questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the product X in the following reaction.
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the acid-catalyzed dehydration of an alcohol. The reactant is 3,3-dimethyl-2-butanol.

Protonation of the hydroxyl group by $H_2SO_4$ to form a good leaving group ($-OH_2^+$).
$CH_3-C(CH_3)_2-CH(OH)-CH_3 + H^+ \rightarrow CH_3-C(CH_3)_2-CH(OH_2^+)-CH_3$

Loss of a water molecule to form a secondary ($2^\circ$) carbocation.
$CH_3-C(CH_3)_2-CH(OH_2^+)-CH_3 \rightarrow CH_3-C(CH_3)_2-CH^+-CH_3 + H_2O$

The $2^\circ$ carbocation undergoes a 1,2-methyl shift to form a more stable tertiary ($3^\circ$) carbocation.
$CH_3-C(CH_3)_2-CH^+-CH_3 \xrightarrow{\text{1,2-methyl shift}} CH_3-C^+(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3$

Elimination of a proton ($H^+$) from the adjacent carbon atom yields the most substituted alkene as the major product, according to Saytzeff's rule.
$CH_3-C^+(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3 \rightarrow CH_3-C(CH_3)=C(CH_3)-CH_3 + H^+$

The major product formed is 2,3-dimethyl-2-butene.

Answer: 2,3-dimethyl-2-butene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following ether, on hydrolysis, gives two different products that are successive members of the homologous series?
questions.solution:
Hydrolysis of an ether $R-O-R'$ yields two alcohol molecules, $R-OH$ and $R'-OH$.

For the products to be successive members of a homologous series, they must differ by exactly one $-CH_2-$ unit. This means the alkyl groups $R$ and $R'$ must differ by one carbon atom.

Methoxymethane ($CH_3-O-CH_3$) gives two molecules of methanol, which are identical.

Methoxypropane ($CH_3-O-C_3H_7$) gives methanol and propanol, which differ by two carbon atoms.

Ethoxypropane ($C_2H_5-O-C_3H_7$) gives ethanol ($C_2H_5OH$) and propanol ($C_3H_7OH$). These are successive members of the alcohol homologous series as they differ by one $-CH_2-$ group.

Answer: Ethoxypropane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reagents limits the oxidation of $\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH}$ up to R-CHO only?
questions.solution:
Primary alcohols ($\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH}$) can be oxidized to aldehydes ($\text{R-CHO}$) or carboxylic acids ($\text{R-COOH}$) depending on the oxidizing agent used.

Strong oxidizing agents like acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$, $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7$ / dil. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, and $\text{CrO}_3$ in aqueous medium oxidize primary alcohols directly to carboxylic acids.

To limit the oxidation to the aldehyde stage, mild oxidizing agents are required. Pyridinium chlorochromate (PCC) is a mild oxidizing agent that selectively oxidizes primary alcohols to aldehydes and prevents further oxidation to carboxylic acids.

$\text{R-CH}_2\text{OH} \xrightarrow{\text{PCC}} \text{R-CHO}$

Answer: PCC

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is action of $\text{CH}_3\text{ONa}$ on $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$
$\text{CH}_3\text{ONa} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \rightarrow$ ?
questions.solution:
The reaction between sodium methoxide ($\text{CH}_3\text{ONa}$) and ethyl bromide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$) is an example of Williamson ether synthesis.

The methoxide ion ($\text{CH}_3\text{O}^{-}$) acts as a nucleophile and attacks the primary alkyl halide ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$) via an $S_N2$ mechanism.

The reaction proceeds as follows:
$\text{CH}_3\text{ONa} + \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaBr}$

The products formed are ethyl methyl ether and sodium bromide.

Answer: Formation of $\text{CH}_3\text{OCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{NaBr}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the name of the above reaction.
questions.solution:
The given reaction shows the conversion of benzene to benzaldehyde using carbon monoxide ($CO$) and hydrogen chloride ($HCl$) in the presence of anhydrous aluminum chloride ($AlCl_3$) under high pressure.

This specific transformation is known as the Gatterman-Koch formylation reaction. In this reaction, a formyl cation is generated in situ from $CO$, $HCl$, and the Lewis acid catalyst ($AlCl_3$), which then undergoes electrophilic aromatic substitution with benzene to form benzaldehyde.

Let us review the other options:
1. Etard reaction: Involves the oxidation of toluene to benzaldehyde using chromyl chloride ($CrO_2Cl_2$).
2. Stephen reaction: Involves the reduction of nitriles to aldehydes using tin(II) chloride ($SnCl_2$) and $HCl$, followed by hydrolysis.
3. Rosenmund reaction: Involves the catalytic hydrogenation of acid chlorides to aldehydes using palladium on barium sulfate ($Pd/BaSO_4$).

Therefore, the correct name for the given reaction is the Gatterman-Koch formylation reaction.

Answer: Gatterman-Koch formylation reaction

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Acetone on heating with $\text{CrO}_3$ mainly forms,
questions.solution:
Ketones are generally resistant to oxidation under normal conditions. However, on vigorous heating with strong oxidizing agents like $\text{CrO}_3$, they undergo cleavage of the C-C bond to form carboxylic acids with fewer carbon atoms.

Acetone ($\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3$) undergoes oxidation to form a two-carbon carboxylic acid and a one-carbon fragment which further oxidizes to carbon dioxide and water.

$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_3 \xrightarrow{\text{CrO}_3, \Delta} \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$

The main product formed is acetic acid.

Answer: Acetic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Tertiary amines have the lowest boiling points because ,
options: They possess inter-molecular dipole-dipole attraction forces.
They do not possess inter-molecular H- bonding
questions.solution:
Tertiary amines have the general formula $R_3N$. Since there are no hydrogen atoms directly attached to the highly electronegative nitrogen atom, they cannot form intermolecular hydrogen bonds.

In contrast, primary and secondary amines have hydrogen atoms attached to nitrogen and can form intermolecular hydrogen bonds, which leads to higher boiling points.

Due to the absence of intermolecular hydrogen bonding, tertiary amines have the lowest boiling points among isomeric amines.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is found to raise the HDL level in the blood?
questions.solution:
Omega-3 fatty acids are polyunsaturated fatty acids that are known to increase the level of High-Density Lipoprotein (HDL), which is considered good cholesterol, in the blood. They also help in lowering triglyceride levels, thereby reducing the risk of cardiovascular diseases.

Trans fats, on the other hand, lower HDL levels and raise LDL (bad cholesterol) levels.

Answer: Omega-3 fatty acids

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The letter 'D' in carbohydrates signifies
questions.solution:
The letters 'D' and 'L' before the name of carbohydrates represent the relative configuration of the molecule with respect to glyceraldehyde.

It does not indicate the optical activity (dextrorotatory or laevorotatory), which is represented by (+) or (-) signs respectively.

Therefore, 'D' signifies configuration.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following molecules is capable of forming Zwitter ion?
questions.solution:
A Zwitter ion is a dipolar ion formed by the internal transfer of a proton from an acidic group to a basic group within the same molecule.

Among the given options, $\text{NH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$ (glycine) is an amino acid that contains both an acidic carboxyl group ($-\text{COOH}$) and a basic amino group ($-\text{NH}_2$).

In aqueous solution, the $-\text{COOH}$ group donates a proton to the $-\text{NH}_2$ group, forming the Zwitter ion $^{+}\text{NH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COO}^{-}$.

The other molecules lack either an acidic or a basic group required for this internal proton transfer.

Answer: $\text{NH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When sodium bicarbonate is added to an organic compound, brisk effervescences is evolved. This indicate the presence of which functional group.
questions.solution:
Sodium bicarbonate ($NaHCO_3$) is a weak base that reacts with compounds more acidic than carbonic acid ($H_2CO_3$).

Carboxylic acids ($-\text{COOH}$) react with sodium bicarbonate to produce sodium carboxylate, water, and carbon dioxide gas.

The reaction is given by:

$R-\text{COOH} + NaHCO_3 \rightarrow R-\text{COONa} + H_2O + CO_2 \uparrow$

The evolution of carbon dioxide ($CO_2$) gas is observed as brisk effervescence. This test is the standard qualitative test used to detect the presence of the carboxylic acid functional group in an organic compound.

Answer: $-\text{COOH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total number of electrons present in bonding and antibonding orbitals respectively in $\text{F}_2$ molecule according to MO theory ?
questions.solution:
The atomic number of fluorine ($\text{F}$) is $9$. Therefore, the total number of electrons in the $\text{F}_2$ molecule is $18$.

According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the electronic configuration of $\text{F}_2$ is:
$\sigma_{1s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{1s}{}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 \sigma^{*}_{2s}{}^2 \sigma_{2p_z}^2 \pi_{2p_x}^2 \pi_{2p_y}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_x}{}^2 \pi^{*}_{2p_y}{}^2$

The electrons present in orbitals without an asterisk are bonding electrons ($N_b$), and those in orbitals with an asterisk are antibonding electrons ($N_a$).

Number of bonding electrons ($N_b$) = $2 (\sigma_{1s}) + 2 (\sigma_{2s}) + 2 (\sigma_{2p_z}) + 2 (\pi_{2p_x}) + 2 (\pi_{2p_y}) = 10$

Number of antibonding electrons ($N_a$) = $2 (\sigma^{*}_{1s}) + 2 (\sigma^{*}_{2s}) + 2 (\pi^{*}_{2p_x}) + 2 (\pi^{*}_{2p_y}) = 8$

Thus, there are $10$ bonding electrons and $8$ antibonding electrons.

Answer: Bonding - 10, Antibonding - 8

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The equation for the rate constant is $k = Ae^{-E_a/RT}$.
A chemical reaction will proceed more rapidly if there is a decrease in
questions.solution:
The rate of a chemical reaction is directly proportional to the rate constant $k$.

According to the Arrhenius equation, $k = Ae^{-E_a/RT}$.

For the reaction to proceed more rapidly, the rate constant $k$ must increase.

A decrease in the activation energy $E_a$ makes the exponent $-E_a/RT$ less negative, which increases the value of $e^{-E_a/RT}$.

Therefore, a decrease in $E_a$ leads to an increase in $k$, making the reaction proceed more rapidly.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: If for a first-order reaction, $[A]_0 = 1.0\ \text{M}$ and $[A]_t = 0.25\ \text{M}$ after 276 s, find the value of the rate constant (k).
questions.solution:
For a first-order reaction, the concentration after $n$ half-lives is given by $[A]_t = \dfrac{[A]_0}{2^n}$.

Given $[A]_0 = 1.0\ \text{M}$ and $[A]_t = 0.25\ \text{M}$, we have:

$0.25 = \dfrac{1.0}{2^n} \Rightarrow 2^n = 4 \Rightarrow n = 2$

Thus, two half-lives have passed in $276\ \text{s}$.

$2 t_{1/2} = 276\ \text{s} \Rightarrow t_{1/2} = 138\ \text{s}$

The rate constant $k$ is given by:

$k = \dfrac{0.693}{t_{1/2}} = \dfrac{0.693}{138}$

$k \approx 0.0050\ \text{s}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The rate law for the reaction $A + B \rightarrow P$ is found to be rate $= k[A]^2[B]$.
The rate constant of the reaction at 300 K is $6.0\ \text{M}^{-2}\text{s}^{-1}$. Calculate the rate of the reaction when $[A] = 1\ \text{M}$ and $[B] = 0.2\ \text{M}$
questions.solution:
Given rate law is $\text{Rate} = k[A]^2[B]$.

Substituting the given values:

$\text{Rate} = 6.0 \times (1)^2 \times 0.2$

$\text{Rate} = 1.2\ \text{M s}^{-1}$

Answer: $1.2\ \text{M s}^{-1}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.q: Identify the most electronegative element by the following.
questions.solution:
Electronegativity is the tendency of an atom to attract a shared pair of electrons towards itself.

According to the Pauling scale, the electronegativity values of the given elements are:
Fluorine: $4.0$
Oxygen: $3.5$
Nitrogen: $3.0$
Chlorine: $3.0$

Fluorine has the highest electronegativity among all elements in the periodic table.

Answer: Fluorine

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number of ligands which are directly bonded to the metal is known as
questions.solution:
The number of ligand donor atoms to which the metal is directly bonded is defined as the co-ordination number of the metal in the complex.

For example, in the complex ion $[PtCl_6]^{2-}$, the co-ordination number of platinum is $6$ because it is directly bonded to six chloride ligands.

Answer: co-ordination number

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the ionization isomer of $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\,\text{Cl}(\text{NO}_2)]\,\text{Cl}$ from the following.
questions.solution:
Ionization isomerism occurs when a ligand inside the coordination sphere is exchanged with an anion outside the coordination sphere (counter ion), resulting in a complex that yields different ions in solution.

In the given complex $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\,\text{Cl}(\text{NO}_2)]\,\text{Cl}$, the counter ion is $\text{Cl}^-$ and the ligands are $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{Cl}^-$, and $\text{NO}_2^-$.

By exchanging the $\text{NO}_2^-$ ligand inside the coordination sphere with the $\text{Cl}^-$ counter ion outside, we get the ionization isomer $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\,\text{Cl}_2]\,(\text{NO}_2)$.

The original complex yields $\text{Cl}^-$ ions in aqueous solution, whereas its ionization isomer yields $\text{NO}_2^-$ ions.

Answer: $[\text{Cr}(\text{H}_2\text{O})_4\,\text{Cl}_2]\,(\text{NO}_2)$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following series of transition elements has general electronic configuration, $[\text{Kr}]\,4d^{1-10}\,5s^{0-2}$?
questions.solution:
The general electronic configuration $[\text{Kr}]\,4d^{1-10}\,5s^{0-2}$ corresponds to the transition elements of the 5th period.

In these elements, the 4d subshell is progressively filled from Yttrium (Y) to Cadmium (Cd).

Since the 4d orbitals are being filled, this series is known as the 4d series of transition elements.

Answer: 4d series elements

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of chromium in the final product when KI reacts with acidified potassium dichromate solution?
questions.solution:
Potassium dichromate ($K_2Cr_2O_7$) acts as a strong oxidizing agent in an acidic medium.

It oxidizes iodide ions ($I^-$) from KI to iodine ($I_2$) and itself gets reduced to chromium(III) ions ($Cr^{3+}$).

The ionic equation for the reaction is:

$Cr_2O_7^{2-} + 14H^+ + 6I^- \rightarrow 2Cr^{3+} + 3I_2 + 7H_2O$

In the final product, chromium is present as $Cr^{3+}$.

Therefore, the oxidation state of chromium in the final product is $+3$.

Answer: $+3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following reactions takes place at anode during the electrolysis of molten NaCl?
questions.solution:
During the electrolysis of molten $\text{NaCl}$, the ions present are $\text{Na}^+$ and $\text{Cl}^-$.

At the anode, oxidation takes place. The chloride ions ($\text{Cl}^-$) migrate to the anode and lose electrons to form chlorine gas.

The reaction at the anode is:
$2\text{Cl}^-_{(l)} \rightarrow \text{Cl}_{2(g)} + 2\text{e}^-$

At the cathode, reduction takes place. The sodium ions ($\text{Na}^+$) migrate to the cathode and gain electrons to form liquid sodium.

The reaction at the cathode is:
$\text{Na}^+_{(l)} + \text{e}^- \rightarrow \text{Na}_{(l)}$

Answer: $2\text{Cl}^-_{(l)} \rightarrow \text{Cl}_{2(g)} + 2\text{e}^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What mass of silver (Atomic mass = 108 g/mol) deposited by a quantity of electricity which displaces 5600 mL of $\text{O}_2$ at STP ?
questions.solution:
Volume of $O_2$ displaced at STP = $5600$ mL = $5.6$ L.

Moles of $O_2$ = $\dfrac{5.6}{22.4} = 0.25$ mol.

The reaction for the liberation of $O_2$ is:
$2H_2O \rightarrow O_2 + 4H^+ + 4e^-$

Number of moles of electrons (Faradays) required for $0.25$ mol of $O_2$ = $0.25 \times 4 = 1$ F.

The reaction for the deposition of silver is:
$Ag^+ + e^- \rightarrow Ag$

Since $1$ F of electricity deposits $1$ mole of Ag, the mass of Ag deposited is:
$1 \times 108 = 108.0$ g.

Answer: $108.0\ \text{g}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of following has the highest nucleophilicity ?
questions.solution:
The given species $\text{CH}_3^-$, $\text{NH}_2^-$, $\text{OH}^-$, and $\text{F}^-$ have donor atoms belonging to the same period (Period 2) of the periodic table.

Across a period from left to right, the electronegativity of the atoms increases in the order $\text{C} \lt \text{N} \lt \text{O} \lt \text{F}$.

A more electronegative atom holds its lone pair of electrons more tightly, making it less available for donation to an electrophile. Therefore, nucleophilicity decreases as electronegativity increases.

The order of nucleophilicity is $\text{CH}_3^- \gt \text{NH}_2^- \gt \text{OH}^- \gt \text{F}^-$.

Thus, $\text{CH}_3^-$ has the highest nucleophilicity.

Answer: $\text{CH}_3^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
What is the product P obtained in following reaction?
$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{AgCN}_{(alc)} \rightarrow \text{P}$
questions.solution:
$\text{AgCN}$ is predominantly a covalent compound. The bond between $\text{Ag}$ and $\text{C}$ is covalent, which leaves the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom available for nucleophilic attack.

When an alkyl halide such as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ reacts with alcoholic $\text{AgCN}$, the nucleophilic attack occurs through the nitrogen atom rather than the carbon atom.

This results in the formation of an alkyl isocyanide as the major product.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br} + \text{AgCN}_{(alc)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC} + \text{AgBr}$

The product P is ethyl isocyanide, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NC}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the reagent used for replacement of $-\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^-$ from benzene diazonium chloride by iodine.
questions.solution:
Benzene diazonium chloride reacts with aqueous potassium iodide (KI) upon warming to form iodobenzene.

The reaction is given by:
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^+\text{Cl}^- + \text{KI} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{I} + \text{N}_2 + \text{KCl}$

Therefore, the reagent used for the replacement of the diazonium group by iodine is KI.

Answer: KI

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the use of Baeyer's reagent by the following.
options: Detecting the presence of carbon carbon double bond.
questions.solution:
Baeyer's reagent is a cold, dilute, alkaline solution of potassium permanganate ($KMnO_4$).

It is a strong oxidizing agent, but its primary application in qualitative organic analysis is to test for unsaturation.

When Baeyer's reagent reacts with an organic compound containing a carbon-carbon double bond (alkene) or triple bond (alkyne), the purple colour of the permanganate solution disappears and a brown precipitate of manganese dioxide ($MnO_2$) is formed.

Therefore, it is used for detecting the presence of carbon-carbon double bonds.

Answer: Detecting the presence of carbon carbon double bond.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the catalyst used in the Friedel crafts acylation reaction.
questions.solution:
Friedel-Crafts acylation is an electrophilic aromatic substitution reaction in which an acyl group is introduced into an aromatic ring.

The reaction requires a strong Lewis acid catalyst to facilitate the generation of the electrophilic acylium ion from an acyl halide or acid anhydride.

Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$ is the standard and most widely used Lewis acid catalyst for this purpose.

The general reaction is:
$\text{ArH} + \text{RCOCl} \xrightarrow{\text{Anhydrous AlCl}_3} \text{ArCOR} + \text{HCl}$

Answer: Anhydrous $\text{AlCl}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is NOT correct regarding dihydrogen?
options: It is colorless and tasteless gas.
It burns with a pale blue flame.
It is a polar water-soluble gas.
questions.solution:
Dihydrogen ($H_2$) is a homonuclear diatomic molecule, meaning both atoms have the same electronegativity. Therefore, it is a non-polar molecule.

Since water is a polar solvent, dihydrogen is practically insoluble in water due to the "like dissolves like" principle.

Dihydrogen is a colorless, odorless, and tasteless gas. It is lighter than air and burns with a pale blue flame.

Thus, the statement that it is a polar water-soluble gas is incorrect.

Answer: It is a polar water-soluble gas.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the role of glycerol in the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide?
options: It increases the enthalpy of the reaction.
It increases the rate of collisions between reactant molecules.
questions.solution:
Hydrogen peroxide ($H_2O_2$) decomposes into water and oxygen gas upon standing or heating.

To prevent or slow down this decomposition, certain substances are added which act as negative catalysts (inhibitors).

Glycerol, along with urea and acetanilide, is commonly used as a stabilizer for hydrogen peroxide. It acts as a negative catalyst and retards the decomposition process.

Therefore, glycerol reduces the reaction rate of the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide.

Answer: It reduces the reaction rate.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify from the following salts an example of a salt of strong acid and weak base.
questions.solution:
Ammonium acetate is a salt of a weak acid (acetic acid) and a weak base (ammonium hydroxide).

Sodium acetate is a salt of a weak acid (acetic acid) and a strong base (sodium hydroxide).

Copper (II) chloride is a salt of a strong acid (hydrochloric acid) and a weak base (copper (II) hydroxide).

Sodium carbonate is a salt of a weak acid (carbonic acid) and a strong base (sodium hydroxide).

Thus, copper (II) chloride is the correct example of a salt of a strong acid and a weak base.

Answer: Copper (II) chloride.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following salt undergoes anionic hydrolysis ?
questions.solution:
Anionic hydrolysis occurs in salts formed by the neutralization of a strong base and a weak acid.

$\text{CuSO}_4$ is a salt of a weak base ($\text{Cu(OH)}_2$) and a strong acid ($\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$). It undergoes cationic hydrolysis.

$\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ is a salt of a strong base ($\text{NaOH}$) and a weak acid ($\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$). The carbonate ion ($\text{CO}_3^{2-}$) undergoes anionic hydrolysis to produce $\text{OH}^-$ ions: $\text{CO}_3^{2-} + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{HCO}_3^- + \text{OH}^-$.

$\text{NH}_4\text{Cl}$ is a salt of a weak base ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$) and a strong acid ($\text{HCl}$). It undergoes cationic hydrolysis.

$\text{FeCl}_3$ is a salt of a weak base ($\text{Fe(OH)}_3$) and a strong acid ($\text{HCl}$). It undergoes cationic hydrolysis.

Thus, $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$ undergoes anionic hydrolysis.

Answer: $\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The solubility product of sparingly soluble salt BA is $4 \times 10^{-13}$. Calculate the $[\text{A}^-]$ if $[\text{B}^+]$ is $1 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{M}$.
questions.solution:
The dissociation of the sparingly soluble salt $\text{BA}$ is given by:

$\text{BA} \rightleftharpoons \text{B}^+ + \text{A}^-$

The solubility product expression is:

$K_{sp} = [\text{B}^+][\text{A}^-]$

Given:

$K_{sp} = 4 \times 10^{-13}$

$[\text{B}^+] = 1 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{M}$

Substituting the given values into the expression:

$4 \times 10^{-13} = (1 \times 10^{-6}) \times [\text{A}^-]$

$[\text{A}^-] = \dfrac{4 \times 10^{-13}}{1 \times 10^{-6}}$

$[\text{A}^-] = 4 \times 10^{-7}\ \text{M}$

Answer: $4 \times 10^{-7}\ \text{M}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Buna-S is prepared from
questions.solution:
Buna-S is a copolymer synthesized from $1,3$-butadiene and styrene in the presence of sodium as a catalyst.

The "Bu" stands for $1,3$-butadiene, "na" stands for sodium, and "S" stands for styrene.

The polymerization reaction involves the addition of $1,3$-butadiene and styrene molecules to form the elastomer Buna-S, which is also known as styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR).

Answer: 1, 3- butadiene and styrene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which polymer is commonly used in nonstick cookwares ?
questions.solution:
Teflon (polytetrafluoroethylene) is chemically inert and highly resistant to heat. It has a very low coefficient of friction, which prevents food from sticking to the surface.

Therefore, Teflon is commonly used as a coating in nonstick cookware.

Answer: Teflon

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the polymer used to prepare plastic bottles needed to store cooking oil.
questions.solution:
Polyethylene terephthalate (PET) is a strong, lightweight, and transparent synthetic resin belonging to the polyester family of polymers.

It provides an excellent barrier to oxygen and moisture, making it highly suitable for food packaging.

PET is widely blow-moulded into disposable plastic bottles used for storing cooking oil, mineral water, and carbonated beverages.

Answer: PET

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following phenomena represents oxidation?
questions.solution:
Oxidation is defined as the addition of oxygen or any other electronegative element, the removal of hydrogen or any other electropositive element, or the loss of electrons.

Removal of oxygen represents reduction.

Addition of an electronegative element represents oxidation.

Addition of an electropositive element represents reduction.

Gain of electrons represents reduction.

Answer: Addition of electronegative element

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is oxidation state of chlorine in chlorous acid?
questions.solution:
The chemical formula of chlorous acid is $HClO_2$.

Let the oxidation state of chlorine be $x$.

The oxidation state of hydrogen is $+1$ and that of oxygen is $-2$.

Since the molecule is neutral, the sum of the oxidation states of all atoms is zero.

$+1 + x + 2(-2) = 0$

$1 + x - 4 = 0$

$x - 3 = 0$

$x = +3$

The oxidation state of chlorine in chlorous acid is $+3$.

Answer: $+3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the coordination number of Ag in a crystal lattice?
questions.solution:
Silver (Ag) crystallizes in a face-centered cubic (fcc) or cubic close-packed (ccp) lattice structure.

In an fcc or ccp lattice, each atom is surrounded by $12$ nearest neighboring atoms ($6$ in its own layer, $3$ in the layer above, and $3$ in the layer below).

Therefore, the coordination number of Ag in its crystal lattice is $12$.

Answer: $12$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When silver crystallizes, it forms face centered cubic cells, if the volume of unit cells $6.84 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$. Calculate the density of silver. (Molar mass of silver is 108 g/mol, $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$)
questions.solution:
For a face-centered cubic (fcc) unit cell, the number of atoms per unit cell is $Z = 4$.

The density of the unit cell is given by the formula:

$d = \dfrac{Z \times M}{N_A \times V}$

Substituting the given values:

$d = \dfrac{4 \times 108}{6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 6.84 \times 10^{-23}}$

$d = \dfrac{432}{41.19}$

$d = 10.49\ \text{gm cm}^{-3}$

Answer: $10.49\ \text{gm cm}^{-3}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the total contribution of all corner particles in bcc unit cell?
questions.solution:
In a body-centered cubic (bcc) unit cell, particles are present at all $8$ corners and $1$ particle is present at the body center.

Each corner particle is shared by $8$ adjacent unit cells. Thus, the contribution of one corner particle to a single unit cell is $\dfrac{1}{8}$.

Since there are $8$ corners in a unit cell, the total contribution of all corner particles is $8 \times \dfrac{1}{8} = 1$ particle.

Answer: 1 particle

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of solution is a brass ?
questions.solution:
Brass is an alloy composed primarily of copper and zinc.

Both the solute (zinc) and the solvent (copper) are in the solid state.

Therefore, brass is an example of a solid in solid solution.

Answer: solid in solid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: 18 g of glucose (molar mass = 180 g/mol) is dissolved in water to prepare 500 ml solution at $15^\circ\text{C}$. Calculate the osmotic pressure of the solution. [$R = 0.0821\ \text{L atm K}^{-1}\ \text{mol}^{-1}$]
questions.solution:
Number of moles of glucose, $n = \dfrac{18}{180} = 0.1\text{ mol}$

Volume of solution, $V = 500\text{ ml} = 0.5\text{ L}$

Temperature, $T = 15 + 273 = 288\text{ K}$

Osmotic pressure is given by $\pi = CRT = \dfrac{n}{V}RT$

Substituting the values:

$\pi = \dfrac{0.1}{0.5} \times 0.0821 \times 288$

$\pi = 0.2 \times 0.0821 \times 288$

$\pi = 4.72896\text{ atm} \approx 4.73\text{ atm}$

Answer: $4.73\ \text{atm}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The normal boiling point of Ethyl acetate is $77^\circ\text{C}$. A solution of non-volatile non-electrolyte solute in ethyl acetate boils at $78^\circ\text{C}$. $K_b$ for ethyl acetate is $2.77\ ^\circ\text{C kg mol}^{-1}$. What is the molality of the solution ?
questions.solution:
The elevation in boiling point is given by $\Delta T_b = T_b - T_b^{\circ}$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta T_b = 78^{\circ}\text{C} - 77^{\circ}\text{C} = 1^{\circ}\text{C}$

For a non-volatile, non-electrolyte solute, the elevation in boiling point is related to molality $m$ by the formula $\Delta T_b = K_b m$

$1 = 2.77 m$

$m = \dfrac{1}{2.77} = 0.361\ \text{m}$

Answer: $0.361\ \text{m}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The ratio of mass of 'x' atoms of an element to mass of carbon atoms is 9:1. Find the mass of 1 mol of x if molar mass of carbon is 12 g/mol.
questions.solution:
Let the mass of one atom of element 'x' be $m_x$ and the mass of one carbon atom be $m_C$.

Given that the ratio of the mass of an atom of element 'x' to the mass of a carbon atom is $9:1$, we have:

$\dfrac{m_x}{m_C} = \dfrac{9}{1}$

The ratio of their molar masses is equal to the ratio of their atomic masses:

$\dfrac{M_x}{M_C} = 9$

Given the molar mass of carbon, $M_C = 12\ \text{g/mol}$, the molar mass of element 'x' is:

$M_x = 9 \times 12 = 108\ \text{g/mol}$

Therefore, the mass of $1\ \text{mol}$ of element 'x' is $108\ \text{g}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: At constant temperature, a gas occupies a volume of 200 mL at a pressure of 500 mm Hg. What will be its volume at 800 mm Hg pressure?
questions.solution:
According to Boyle's law, at constant temperature, $P_1 V_1 = P_2 V_2$.

Given $P_1 = 500\ \text{mm Hg}$, $V_1 = 200\ \text{mL}$, and $P_2 = 800\ \text{mm Hg}$.

Substituting the values:

$500 \times 200 = 800 \times V_2$

$V_2 = \dfrac{500 \times 200}{800} = 125\ \text{mL}$

Answer: $125\ \text{mL}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of unpaired electrons present in ground state of Silicon and Chromium, respectively ?
questions.solution:
The atomic number of Silicon (Si) is $14$.

The electronic configuration of Si is $1s^{2} 2s^{2} 2p^{6} 3s^{2} 3p^{2}$.

In the $3p$ subshell, there are $2$ electrons which occupy separate orbitals according to Hund's rule. Thus, Si has $2$ unpaired electrons.

The atomic number of Chromium (Cr) is $24$.

The electronic configuration of Cr is $[Ar] 3d^{5} 4s^{1}$.

In the $3d$ subshell, there are $5$ unpaired electrons and in the $4s$ subshell, there is $1$ unpaired electron. Thus, Cr has $6$ unpaired electrons.

The number of unpaired electrons in Si and Cr are $2$ and $6$, respectively.

Answer: 2 and 6

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the process that proceeds with no heat exchange between system and surrounding.
questions.solution:
An adiabatic process is defined as a thermodynamic process in which there is no heat exchange between the system and its surroundings. In this process, $q = 0$.

An isothermal process occurs at constant temperature ($\Delta T = 0$).

An isobaric process occurs at constant pressure ($\Delta P = 0$).

An isochoric process occurs at constant volume ($\Delta V = 0$).

Answer: Adiabatic

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Calculate the enthalpy change when 6 g. $\text{CO(g)}$ reacts with sufficient $\text{NO}_2\text{(g)}$ according to the following reaction
$4\,\text{CO(g)} + 2\,\text{NO}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow 4\,\text{CO}_2\text{(g)} + 2\text{N}_2\text{(g)}\,;\ \Delta_r H^0 = -1200\ \text{kJ}$
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\text{CO} = 12 + 16 = 28\ \text{g mol}^{-1}$

Number of moles of $\text{CO} = \dfrac{6}{28} = \dfrac{3}{14}\ \text{mol}$

From the given balanced equation, the enthalpy change for the reaction of $4\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{CO}$ is $-1200\ \text{kJ}$.

Enthalpy change for $1\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{CO} = \dfrac{-1200}{4} = -300\ \text{kJ}$

Enthalpy change for $\dfrac{3}{14}\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{CO} = -300 \times \dfrac{3}{14} = -64.285\ \text{kJ} \approx -64.29\ \text{kJ}$

Answer: $-64.29\ \text{kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The heat of combustion of carbon to $\text{CO}_2$ is $-393.5\ \text{kJ/mol}$. The heat released upon formation of 35.2 g of $\text{CO}_2$ from carbon and oxygen gas is
questions.solution:
The combustion reaction of carbon is given by:

$\text{C(s)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CO}_2\text{(g)}$

The heat of combustion of carbon to $\text{CO}_2$ is $\Delta H = -393.5\ \text{kJ/mol}$.

Molar mass of $\text{CO}_2 = 12 + 2 \times 16 = 44\ \text{g/mol}$.

Number of moles in $35.2\ \text{g}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ is:

$n = \dfrac{35.2}{44} = 0.8\ \text{mol}$

The enthalpy change for the formation of $0.8\ \text{mol}$ of $\text{CO}_2$ is:

$\Delta H = 0.8\ \text{mol} \times (-393.5\ \text{kJ/mol}) = -314.8\ \text{kJ} \approx -315\ \text{kJ}$

The negative sign indicates that the heat is released during the process.

Answer: $-315\ \text{kJ}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements is not correct ?
options: For a chemical reaction to be spontaneous $\Delta G$ must be $-\text{ve}$.
Electrical work is equal to $\Delta G$
questions.solution:
Gibbs free energy ($G$) and standard Gibbs free energy change ($\Delta G^\circ$) depend on the quantity of the substance, hence they are extensive properties.

Standard cell potential ($E^\circ_{\text{cell}}$) is independent of the amount of substance, hence it is an intensive property.

For a spontaneous reaction at constant temperature and pressure, the change in Gibbs free energy ($\Delta G$) must be negative ($\Delta G \lt 0$).

The reversible electrical work done by a galvanic cell is equal to the decrease in its Gibbs free energy. Therefore, electrical work done by the system is equal to $-\Delta G$, not $\Delta G$.

Thus, the statement "Electrical work is equal to $\Delta G$" is incorrect.

Answer: Electrical work is equal to $\Delta G$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of tangent to the curves $x = 1 - 3t^2$ and $y = t - 3t^3$ at the point $(-2, 2)$ is...
questions.solution:
Given $x = 1 - 3t^2$ and $y = t - 3t^3$.

At the point $(-2, 2)$, we have $1 - 3t^2 = -2 \Rightarrow 3t^2 = 3 \Rightarrow t = \pm 1$.

Also $t - 3t^3 = 2$. For $t = -1$, $-1 - 3(-1)^3 = 2$, which satisfies the equation. Thus, $t = -1$.

Differentiating $x$ and $y$ with respect to $t$:

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = -6t$

$\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 1 - 9t^2$

The slope of the tangent is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\dfrac{dy}{dt}}{\dfrac{dx}{dt}} = \dfrac{1 - 9t^2}{-6t}$.

At $t = -1$, $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1 - 9(-1)^2}{-6(-1)} = \dfrac{-8}{6} = -\dfrac{4}{3}$.

The equation of the tangent at $(-2, 2)$ is:

$y - 2 = -\dfrac{4}{3}(x - (-2))$

$3(y - 2) = -4(x + 2)$

$3y - 6 = -4x - 8$

$4x + 3y + 2 = 0$

Answer: $4x + 3y + 2 = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A spherical snow ball is melting so that its volume is decreasing at the rate of 8 c.c./sec then the rate of change of radius when the radius is 2 cm, is :
options: The radius is increasing at the rate of $\dfrac{1}{2\pi}\ \text{cm/s}$
The radius is decreasing at the rate of $\dfrac{1}{2\pi}\ \text{cm/s}$
The radius is increasing at the rate of $\dfrac{1}{\pi}\ \text{cm/s}$
The radius is decreasing at the rate of $\dfrac{1}{\pi}\ \text{cm/s}$
questions.solution:
Let $V$ be the volume and $r$ be the radius of the spherical snowball.

$V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$

Differentiating with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^2 \dfrac{dr}{dt}$

Given that the volume is decreasing at the rate of $8$ c.c./sec, $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -8$ cm$^3$/sec.

Substituting $r = 2$ cm and $\dfrac{dV}{dt} = -8$:

$-8 = 4\pi (2)^2 \dfrac{dr}{dt}$

$-8 = 16\pi \dfrac{dr}{dt}$

$\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -\dfrac{1}{2\pi}$ cm/sec

The negative sign indicates that the radius is decreasing at the rate of $\dfrac{1}{2\pi}$ cm/s.

Answer: The radius is decreasing at the rate of $\dfrac{1}{2\pi}\ \text{cm/s}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A cylindrical tank without a top lid is being manufactured to hold a fixed volume of $125\pi$ cubic cm. The minimum surface area required to construct this tank is ............square cm
questions.solution:
Let $r$ be the radius and $h$ be the height of the cylindrical tank.

Given the volume $V = \pi r^2 h = 125\pi$

$\Rightarrow h = \dfrac{125}{r^2}$

The surface area of the tank without a top lid is $S = 2\pi r h + \pi r^2$

Substituting the value of $h$, we get:

$S = 2\pi r \left(\dfrac{125}{r^2}\right) + \pi r^2 = \dfrac{250\pi}{r} + \pi r^2$

To find the minimum surface area, we differentiate $S$ with respect to $r$ and equate it to zero:

$\dfrac{dS}{dr} = -\dfrac{250\pi}{r^2} + 2\pi r = 0$

$\Rightarrow 2\pi r = \dfrac{250\pi}{r^2}$

$\Rightarrow r^3 = 125 \Rightarrow r = 5$

Also, $\dfrac{d^2S}{dr^2} = \dfrac{500\pi}{r^3} + 2\pi \gt 0$ for $r = 5$, which confirms a minimum.

The minimum surface area is:

$S = \dfrac{250\pi}{5} + \pi (5)^2 = 50\pi + 25\pi = 75\pi$

Answer: $75\pi$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region common to the parabolas $4y^2 = 9x$ and $3x^2 = 16y$ is...
questions.solution:
The given equations of the parabolas are $4y^2 = 9x$ and $3x^2 = 16y$.

From the second equation, we have $y = \dfrac{3x^2}{16}$. Substituting this into the first equation:

$4\left(\dfrac{3x^2}{16}\right)^2 = 9x$

$\dfrac{9x^4}{64} = 9x$

$x^4 - 64x = 0$

$x(x^3 - 64) = 0$

The real roots are $x = 0$ and $x = 4$.

The required area $A$ is the integral of the upper curve minus the lower curve from $x = 0$ to $x = 4$:

$A = \int_{0}^{4} \left( \dfrac{3}{2}\sqrt{x} - \dfrac{3x^2}{16} \right) dx$

$A = \left[ x^{3/2} - \dfrac{x^3}{16} \right]_{0}^{4}$

$A = \left( 4^{3/2} - \dfrac{4^3}{16} \right) - 0$

$A = 8 - 4 = 4$ sq. units.

Answer: 4 sq. units

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area of the region enclosed by the lines $y = 2x, 2y = x$ and $x = 2$ (in sq.units) is...
questions.solution:
The given lines are $y = 2x$, $y = \dfrac{x}{2}$, and $x = 2$.

The points of intersection of the lines are $(0,0)$, $(2,4)$, and $(2,1)$.

The region is bounded by the upper line $y = 2x$ and the lower line $y = \dfrac{x}{2}$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$.

The area of the region is given by the integral of the difference between the upper and lower curves:

$\text{Area} = \int_{0}^{2} \left(2x - \dfrac{x}{2}\right) dx$

$\text{Area} = \int_{0}^{2} \dfrac{3x}{2} dx$

$\text{Area} = \left[ \dfrac{3x^2}{4} \right]_{0}^{2}$

$\text{Area} = \dfrac{3(2)^2}{4} - 0 = 3$

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Line $l : x + y = 4$ intersects the circle $x^2 + y^2 - 2x - 2y = 2$ at points $A$ and $B$. If C is the center of the circle, then the area of $\triangle ABC$ is...
questions.solution:
Equation of the circle is $x^2 + y^2 - 2x - 2y = 2$, which can be written as $(x-1)^2 + (y-1)^2 = 4$.

Center of the circle is $C(1, 1)$ and radius is $R = 2$.

The perpendicular distance $d$ from the center $C(1, 1)$ to the line $x + y - 4 = 0$ is given by $d = \dfrac{|1 + 1 - 4|}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2}} = \sqrt{2}$.

The length of the chord $AB$ is $2\sqrt{R^2 - d^2} = 2\sqrt{2^2 - (\sqrt{2})^2} = 2\sqrt{2}$.

The area of $\triangle ABC$ is $\dfrac{1}{2} \times AB \times d = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2} = 2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $n$ is a positive integer, then $(1 + i\sqrt{3})^{2n} + (1 - i\sqrt{3})^{2n}$ is equal to .........
questions.solution:
Let $z = 1 + i\sqrt{3}$.

Converting to polar form, we have $r = \sqrt{1^2 + (\sqrt{3})^2} = 2$ and $\theta = \tan^{-1}(\sqrt{3}) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$.

Thus, $1 + i\sqrt{3} = 2\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} + i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$.

Similarly, $1 - i\sqrt{3} = 2\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} - i\sin\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$.

Using De Moivre's theorem, we get:

$(1 + i\sqrt{3})^{2n} = 2^{2n}\left(\cos\dfrac{2n\pi}{3} + i\sin\dfrac{2n\pi}{3}\right)$

$(1 - i\sqrt{3})^{2n} = 2^{2n}\left(\cos\dfrac{2n\pi}{3} - i\sin\dfrac{2n\pi}{3}\right)$

Adding the two expressions:

$(1 + i\sqrt{3})^{2n} + (1 - i\sqrt{3})^{2n} = 2^{2n}\left(2\cos\dfrac{2n\pi}{3}\right) = 2^{2n+1}\cos\dfrac{2n\pi}{3}$.

Answer: $2^{2n+1}\cos\left(\dfrac{2n\pi}{3}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the function f is continuous at $x = \pi$, where $f(x) = \dfrac{1 - \cos[7(x - \pi)]}{5(x - \pi)^2}$, for $x \neq \pi$, then $f(\pi) = $
questions.solution:
Since the function $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = \pi$, $f(\pi) = \lim_{x \rightarrow \pi} f(x)$.

Substituting $t = x - \pi$, as $x \rightarrow \pi$, $t \rightarrow 0$.

$f(\pi) = \lim_{t \rightarrow 0} \dfrac{1 - \cos(7t)}{5t^2}$

Using the identity $1 - \cos \theta = 2 \sin^2\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$:

$f(\pi) = \lim_{t \rightarrow 0} \dfrac{2 \sin^2\left(\dfrac{7t}{2}\right)}{5t^2}$

$f(\pi) = \dfrac{2}{5} \lim_{t \rightarrow 0} \left( \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{7t}{2}\right)}{t} \right)^2$

$f(\pi) = \dfrac{2}{5} \times \left(\dfrac{7}{2}\right)^2 \lim_{t \rightarrow 0} \left( \dfrac{\sin\left(\dfrac{7t}{2}\right)}{\dfrac{7t}{2}} \right)^2$

Since $\lim_{\theta \rightarrow 0} \dfrac{\sin \theta}{\theta} = 1$:

$f(\pi) = \dfrac{2}{5} \times \dfrac{49}{4} \times 1 = \dfrac{49}{10}$

Answer: $\dfrac{49}{10}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\dfrac{2x(1 + \sin x)}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$ is...
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\dfrac{2x(1 + \sin x)}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$

Splitting the integral, we get:

$I = \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\dfrac{2x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx + \int_{-\pi}^{\pi}\dfrac{2x \sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$

The first integral is zero because the integrand $f(x) = \dfrac{2x}{1 + \cos^2 x}$ is an odd function.

The second integral has an even integrand, so:

$I = 2 \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{2x \sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx = 4 \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{x \sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$

Using the property $\int_{0}^{a}f(x)dx = \int_{0}^{a}f(a-x)dx$, we get:

$I = 4 \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{(\pi - x) \sin(\pi - x)}{1 + \cos^2(\pi - x)}dx = 4 \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{(\pi - x) \sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$

Adding the two expressions for $I$:

$2I = 4 \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{\pi \sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$

$I = 2\pi \int_{0}^{\pi}\dfrac{\sin x}{1 + \cos^2 x}dx$

Substituting $\cos x = t$, we get $-\sin x dx = dt$. The limits change from $1$ to $-1$:

$I = 2\pi \int_{1}^{-1}\dfrac{-dt}{1 + t^2} = 2\pi \int_{-1}^{1}\dfrac{dt}{1 + t^2}$

$I = 2\pi [\tan^{-1} t]_{-1}^{1} = 2\pi \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)$

$I = 2\pi \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = \pi^2$

Answer: $\pi^2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of integral $\int_0^1\cot^{-1}(1 + x^2 - x)\,dx$ is...
questions.solution:
$I = \int_0^1 \cot^{-1}(1 + x^2 - x) \, dx$

$I = \int_0^1 \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{1 + x(x - 1)}\right) \, dx$

$I = \int_0^1 \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{x - (x - 1)}{1 + x(x - 1)}\right) \, dx$

$I = \int_0^1 (\tan^{-1}x - \tan^{-1}(x - 1)) \, dx$

Using the property $\int_0^a f(x) \, dx = \int_0^a f(a - x) \, dx$ on the second term:

$\int_0^1 \tan^{-1}(x - 1) \, dx = \int_0^1 \tan^{-1}(1 - x - 1) \, dx = \int_0^1 \tan^{-1}(-x) \, dx = -\int_0^1 \tan^{-1}x \, dx$

$I = \int_0^1 \tan^{-1}x \, dx - \left(-\int_0^1 \tan^{-1}x \, dx\right) = 2\int_0^1 \tan^{-1}x \, dx$

Using integration by parts:

$I = 2 \left[ x \tan^{-1}x \right]_0^1 - 2 \int_0^1 \dfrac{x}{1 + x^2} \, dx$

$I = 2 \left( 1 \cdot \dfrac{\pi}{4} - 0 \right) - \left[ \log(1 + x^2) \right]_0^1$

$I = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \log 2$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \log 2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x)$ is a polynomial such that $f(x) = [f'(x)]^2$ and $f(2) = 0$, then $f(-2) = \ldots$
questions.solution:
Let the degree of the polynomial $f(x)$ be $n$.

The degree of $f'(x)$ is $n-1$, so the degree of $[f'(x)]^2$ is $2(n-1)$.

Equating the degrees, $n = 2n - 2 \Rightarrow n = 2$.

Let $f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c$, where $a \neq 0$.

Then $f'(x) = 2ax + b$.

Substituting into the given equation $f(x) = [f'(x)]^2$:

$ax^2 + bx + c = (2ax + b)^2$

$ax^2 + bx + c = 4a^2x^2 + 4abx + b^2$

Comparing the coefficients of like powers of $x$:

$a = 4a^2 \Rightarrow a = \dfrac{1}{4}$ (since $a \neq 0$)

$b = 4ab \Rightarrow b = b$

$c = b^2$

Thus, the polynomial is $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{4}x^2 + bx + b^2$.

Given $f(2) = 0$:

$\dfrac{1}{4}(2)^2 + 2b + b^2 = 0$

$b^2 + 2b + 1 = 0$

$(b+1)^2 = 0 \Rightarrow b = -1$

Substituting $b = -1$ into $f(x)$:

$f(x) = \dfrac{1}{4}x^2 - x + 1$

Now, evaluating $f(-2)$:

$f(-2) = \dfrac{1}{4}(-2)^2 - (-2) + 1$

$f(-2) = 1 + 2 + 1 = 4$

Answer: $4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the curve passing through the point (0, 1) and having a slope of the tangent at point $P(x, y)$ is equal to $\dfrac{y}{x + y}$, is
questions.solution:
Given the slope of the tangent is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y}{x + y}$

Taking the reciprocal, we get:

$\dfrac{dx}{dy} = \dfrac{x + y}{y}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{dx}{dy} - \dfrac{x}{y} = 1$

This is a linear differential equation of the form $\dfrac{dx}{dy} + Px = Q$, where $P = -\dfrac{1}{y}$ and $Q = 1$.

Integrating Factor (IF) $= e^{\int -\dfrac{1}{y} dy} = e^{-\ln y} = \dfrac{1}{y}$

The solution is given by:

$x \cdot (\text{IF}) = \int Q \cdot (\text{IF}) dy + C$

$\Rightarrow x \left(\dfrac{1}{y}\right) = \int \dfrac{1}{y} dy + C$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{x}{y} = \ln y + C$

Since the curve passes through the point $(0, 1)$, substitute $x = 0$ and $y = 1$:

$\dfrac{0}{1} = \ln 1 + C \Rightarrow C = 0$

Therefore, the equation of the curve is:

$\dfrac{x}{y} = \ln y$

$\Rightarrow y = e^{\dfrac{x}{y}}$

Answer: $y = e^{\frac{x}{y}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If water at $100^\circ\text{C}$ cools in 10 minutes to $80^\circ\text{C}$ and to $65^\circ\text{C}$ in the next 10 minutes, then the room temperature will be ...
questions.solution:
Using Newton's law of cooling:

$\dfrac{T_1 - T_2}{t} = K \left( \dfrac{T_1 + T_2}{2} - T_0 \right)$

For the first $10$ minutes:

$\dfrac{100 - 80}{10} = K \left( \dfrac{100 + 80}{2} - T_0 \right)$

$2 = K(90 - T_0)$

For the next $10$ minutes:

$\dfrac{80 - 65}{10} = K \left( \dfrac{80 + 65}{2} - T_0 \right)$

$1.5 = K(72.5 - T_0)$

Dividing the two equations:

$\dfrac{2}{1.5} = \dfrac{90 - T_0}{72.5 - T_0}$

$\dfrac{4}{3} = \dfrac{90 - T_0}{72.5 - T_0}$

$4(72.5 - T_0) = 3(90 - T_0)$

$290 - 4T_0 = 270 - 3T_0$

$T_0 = 20^\circ\text{C}$

Answer: $20^\circ\text{C}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: For the differential equation $\dfrac{d^3y}{dx^3} + \cos\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right) = 0$, which of the following is true ?
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $\dfrac{d^3y}{dx^3} + \cos\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right) = 0$.

The order of a differential equation is the order of the highest derivative appearing in it. The highest order derivative present is $\dfrac{d^3y}{dx^3}$, so the order is $3$.

The degree of a differential equation is defined only when it can be expressed as a polynomial equation in its derivatives. Since the equation contains the term $\cos\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)$, it cannot be expressed as a polynomial in terms of the derivatives.

Therefore, the degree of the given differential equation is not defined.

Answer: Order = 3, degree is not defined

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - 4^x}{1 + 4^x}\right)$, then $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ at $x = 1$ is
questions.solution:
Given $y = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - 4^x}{1 + 4^x}\right)$

Let $2^x = \tan \theta$. Then $4^x = (2^x)^2 = \tan^2 \theta$.

Substituting this in the given expression:

$y = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 - \tan^2 \theta}{1 + \tan^2 \theta}\right)$

$y = \cos^{-1}(\cos 2\theta)$

Since $2^x \gt 0$, $\tan \theta \gt 0 \Rightarrow \theta \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \Rightarrow 2\theta \in (0, \pi)$.

Thus, $y = 2\theta = 2\tan^{-1}(2^x)$.

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2 \cdot \dfrac{1}{1 + (2^x)^2} \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}(2^x)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2}{1 + 4^x} \cdot 2^x \log 2$

At $x = 1$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2}{1 + 4^1} \cdot 2^1 \log 2 = \dfrac{4\log 2}{5}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4\log 2}{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\cot[f(x)] = \dfrac{3x - x^3}{1 - 3x^2}$ and $\sin[g(x)] = \dfrac{1 - x^2}{1 + x^2}$, then $\lim\limits_{x \to t}\dfrac{f(x) - f(t)}{g(x) - g(t)} = \ldots$
questions.solution:
Given $\cot[f(x)] = \dfrac{3x - x^3}{1 - 3x^2}$

Substituting $x = \tan\theta$, we get:

$\cot[f(x)] = \dfrac{3\tan\theta - \tan^3\theta}{1 - 3\tan^2\theta} = \tan(3\theta)$

$\cot[f(x)] = \cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 3\theta\right)$

$\Rightarrow f(x) = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 3\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 3\tan^{-1}x$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{-3}{1 + x^2}$

Similarly, given $\sin[g(x)] = \dfrac{1 - x^2}{1 + x^2}$

Substituting $x = \tan\theta$, we get:

$\sin[g(x)] = \dfrac{1 - \tan^2\theta}{1 + \tan^2\theta} = \cos(2\theta)$

$\sin[g(x)] = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - 2\theta\right)$

$\Rightarrow g(x) = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 2\theta = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - 2\tan^{-1}x$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$g'(x) = \dfrac{-2}{1 + x^2}$

The given limit is in the form of the definition of the derivative (or can be evaluated using L'Hospital's Rule):

$\lim\limits_{x \to t}\dfrac{f(x) - f(t)}{g(x) - g(t)} = \dfrac{f'(t)}{g'(t)}$

Substituting the derivatives at $x = t$:

$\dfrac{f'(t)}{g'(t)} = \dfrac{\dfrac{-3}{1 + t^2}}{\dfrac{-2}{1 + t^2}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let f(x) be a twice differentiable function such that $f''(x) = -f(x)$, $f'(x) = g(x)$ and $h(x) = \{f(x)\}^2 + \{g(x)\}^2$. If $h(5) = 11$, then $h(10)$ is equal to ...
questions.solution:
Given $h(x) = (f(x))^2 + (g(x))^2$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$h'(x) = 2f(x)f'(x) + 2g(x)g'(x)$

Given $f'(x) = g(x)$, differentiating gives $f''(x) = g'(x)$.

Also given $f''(x) = -f(x)$, so $g'(x) = -f(x)$.

Substituting these into $h'(x)$:

$h'(x) = 2f(x)g(x) + 2g(x)(-f(x)) = 0$

Since $h'(x) = 0$, $h(x)$ is a constant function.

Given $h(5) = 11$, it follows that $h(10) = 11$.

Answer: $11$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $e^x + e^{f(x)} = e$, then the domain of $f(x)$ is
questions.solution:
Given $e^x + e^{f(x)} = e$

$e^{f(x)} = e - e^x$

Taking natural logarithm on both sides, we get

$f(x) = \ln(e - e^x)$

For $f(x)$ to be defined, the argument of the logarithm must be strictly positive.

$e - e^x \gt 0$

$e^x \lt e$

$x \lt 1$

Therefore, the domain of $f(x)$ is $(-\infty, 1)$.

Answer: $(-\infty, 1)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f\left(\dfrac{x-1}{x+1}\right) = x + 1$, then $\int f(x)\,dx = \cdots$
questions.solution:
Let $t = \dfrac{x-1}{x+1}$

$t(x+1) = x-1$

$tx + t = x - 1$

$x(1-t) = t+1$

$x = \dfrac{t+1}{1-t}$

Substituting $x$ in the given equation:

$f(t) = \dfrac{t+1}{1-t} + 1$

$f(t) = \dfrac{t+1+1-t}{1-t} = \dfrac{2}{1-t}$

Replacing $t$ with $x$:

$f(x) = \dfrac{2}{1-x}$

Integrating with respect to $x$:

$\int f(x)\,dx = \int \dfrac{2}{1-x}\,dx$

$\int f(x)\,dx = -2\log|1-x| + c$

Answer: $-2\log|1 - x| + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $a  \gt  0, b  \gt  0$ and $\int\dfrac{1}{ax^2 + b}dx = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}x}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + c$, then $\int\dfrac{1}{bx^2 + a}dx = \ldots$
questions.solution:
We know that $\int\dfrac{1}{ax^2 + b}dx = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{ab}}\tan^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{a}{b}}x\right) + c$

Comparing this with the given expression $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}x}{\sqrt{3}}\right) + c$, we get:

$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{ab}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}} \Rightarrow ab = 6$

$\sqrt{\dfrac{a}{b}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}} \Rightarrow \dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Multiplying the two equations, we get $a^2 = 4 \Rightarrow a = 2$ (since $a \gt 0$).

Substituting $a = 2$ in $ab = 6$, we get $b = 3$.

Now, we need to evaluate $\int\dfrac{1}{bx^2 + a}dx$:

$\int\dfrac{1}{3x^2 + 2}dx = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3 \times 2}}\tan^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}x\right) + c$

$= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}x}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + c$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{6}}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}x}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\int\dfrac{x^4 + 1}{x^6 + 1}dx = $
questions.solution:
The given integral is $I = \int \dfrac{x^4 + 1}{x^6 + 1} dx$

The denominator can be factored as $x^6 + 1 = (x^2)^3 + 1 = (x^2 + 1)(x^4 - x^2 + 1)$

Rewriting the numerator as $x^4 + 1 = (x^4 - x^2 + 1) + x^2$

$I = \int \dfrac{(x^4 - x^2 + 1) + x^2}{(x^2 + 1)(x^4 - x^2 + 1)} dx$

Separating the terms:

$I = \int \dfrac{x^4 - x^2 + 1}{(x^2 + 1)(x^4 - x^2 + 1)} dx + \int \dfrac{x^2}{x^6 + 1} dx$

$I = \int \dfrac{1}{x^2 + 1} dx + \dfrac{1}{3} \int \dfrac{3x^2}{(x^3)^2 + 1} dx$

Substituting $t = x^3 \Rightarrow dt = 3x^2 dx$ in the second integral:

$I = \tan^{-1}x + \dfrac{1}{3} \int \dfrac{1}{t^2 + 1} dt$

$I = \tan^{-1}x + \dfrac{1}{3} \tan^{-1}(t) + c$

$I = \tan^{-1}x + \dfrac{1}{3} \tan^{-1}(x^3) + c$

Answer: $\tan^{-1}x + \dfrac{1}{3}\tan^{-1}(x^3) + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $f(x) = \cos x$, then the value of $\int\dfrac{e^{f(x)}(x\sin^3 x + f(x))}{1 - (f(x))^2}dx = $
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = \cos x$.

Substituting $f(x)$ into the integral, we get:

$I = \int \dfrac{e^{\cos x}(x\sin^3 x + \cos x)}{1 - \cos^2 x} dx$

$I = \int \dfrac{e^{\cos x}(x\sin^3 x + \cos x)}{\sin^2 x} dx$

$I = \int e^{\cos x} \left( x\sin x + \dfrac{\cos x}{\sin^2 x} \right) dx$

$I = \int e^{\cos x} (x\sin x + \text{cosec}\ x \cot x) dx$

We know that $\dfrac{d}{dx} \left( e^{\cos x} g(x) \right) = e^{\cos x} (g'(x) - g(x)\sin x)$.

Let $g'(x) - g(x)\sin x = x\sin x + \text{cosec}\ x \cot x$.

By observation, if we choose $g(x) = -x - \text{cosec}\ x$, then:

$g'(x) = -1 + \text{cosec}\ x \cot x$

$-g(x)\sin x = (x + \text{cosec}\ x)\sin x = x\sin x + 1$

Adding these gives:

$g'(x) - g(x)\sin x = -1 + \text{cosec}\ x \cot x + x\sin x + 1 = x\sin x + \text{cosec}\ x \cot x$.

Thus, the integral evaluates to $e^{\cos x} g(x) + c$.

$I = e^{\cos x} (-x - \text{cosec}\ x) + c$

Substituting back $f(x) = \cos x$:

$I = e^{f(x)} (-\text{cosec}\ x - x) + c$

Answer: $e^{f(x)}(-\text{cosec}\ x - x) + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $(\tan^{-1}x)^2 + (\cot^{-1}x)^2 = \dfrac{5\pi^2}{8}$, then the value of $x$ is equal to...
questions.solution:
Let $\tan^{-1}x = t$. Then $\cot^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - t$.

Substituting in the given equation:

$t^2 + \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - t\right)^2 = \dfrac{5\pi^2}{8}$

$2t^2 - \pi t + \dfrac{\pi^2}{4} - \dfrac{5\pi^2}{8} = 0$

$2t^2 - \pi t - \dfrac{3\pi^2}{8} = 0$

$16t^2 - 8\pi t - 3\pi^2 = 0$

$(4t - 3\pi)(4t + \pi) = 0$

$t = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ or $t = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Since the principal value branch of $\tan^{-1}x$ is $\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, $t = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$ is rejected.

Therefore, $\tan^{-1}x = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$x = \tan\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = -1$

Answer: $-1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\cot^{-1}\left[\dfrac{\sqrt{1 - \sin x} + \sqrt{1 + \sin x}}{\sqrt{1 - \sin x} - \sqrt{1 + \sin x}}\right]$, where $x \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is...
questions.solution:
We know that $1 \pm \sin x = \left(\cos \dfrac{x}{2} \pm \sin \dfrac{x}{2}\right)^2$.

Since $x \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$, we have $\dfrac{x}{2} \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$.

In this interval, $\cos \dfrac{x}{2} \gt \sin \dfrac{x}{2} \gt 0$.

Therefore, $\sqrt{1 - \sin x} = \cos \dfrac{x}{2} - \sin \dfrac{x}{2}$ and $\sqrt{1 + \sin x} = \cos \dfrac{x}{2} + \sin \dfrac{x}{2}$.

Substituting these values into the given expression:

$\dfrac{\sqrt{1 - \sin x} + \sqrt{1 + \sin x}}{\sqrt{1 - \sin x} - \sqrt{1 + \sin x}} = \dfrac{\left(\cos \dfrac{x}{2} - \sin \dfrac{x}{2}\right) + \left(\cos \dfrac{x}{2} + \sin \dfrac{x}{2}\right)}{\left(\cos \dfrac{x}{2} - \sin \dfrac{x}{2}\right) - \left(\cos \dfrac{x}{2} + \sin \dfrac{x}{2}\right)}$

$= \dfrac{2\cos \dfrac{x}{2}}{-2\sin \dfrac{x}{2}} = -\cot \dfrac{x}{2}$

The given expression becomes $\cot^{-1}\left(-\cot \dfrac{x}{2}\right)$.

Using the property $\cot^{-1}(-y) = \pi - \cot^{-1}y$:

$\cot^{-1}\left(-\cot \dfrac{x}{2}\right) = \pi - \cot^{-1}\left(\cot \dfrac{x}{2}\right)$

Since $\dfrac{x}{2} \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$, $\cot^{-1}\left(\cot \dfrac{x}{2}\right) = \dfrac{x}{2}$.

Thus, the value is $\pi - \dfrac{x}{2}$.

Answer: $\pi - \dfrac{x}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\lim\limits_{x \to 0}\dfrac{45^x - 9^x - 5^x + 1}{(k^x - 1)(3^x - 1)} = 2$, then the value of $k$ is ...
questions.solution:
The given limit is $\lim\limits_{x \to 0}\dfrac{45^x - 9^x - 5^x + 1}{(k^x - 1)(3^x - 1)} = 2$

Factorizing the numerator:

$45^x - 9^x - 5^x + 1 = 9^x(5^x - 1) - 1(5^x - 1) = (9^x - 1)(5^x - 1)$

Substituting this back into the limit:

$\lim\limits_{x \to 0}\dfrac{(9^x - 1)(5^x - 1)}{(k^x - 1)(3^x - 1)} = 2$

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $x^2$:

$\lim\limits_{x \to 0}\dfrac{\dfrac{9^x - 1}{x} \cdot \dfrac{5^x - 1}{x}}{\dfrac{k^x - 1}{x} \cdot \dfrac{3^x - 1}{x}} = 2$

Using the standard limit $\lim\limits_{x \to 0}\dfrac{a^x - 1}{x} = \ln a$, we get:

$\dfrac{\ln 9 \cdot \ln 5}{\ln k \cdot \ln 3} = 2$

Since $\ln 9 = \ln(3^2) = 2 \ln 3$, the equation becomes:

$\dfrac{2 \ln 3 \cdot \ln 5}{\ln k \cdot \ln 3} = 2$

$\dfrac{2 \ln 5}{\ln k} = 2$

$\ln k = \ln 5$

$k = 5$

Answer: $5$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The minimum value of $z = 3x + 5y$, subject to constraints $x \leq 80$, $y \geq 60$, $x + y \leq 200$ & $x, y \geq 0$ occurs at the point...
questions.solution:
The given objective function is $z = 3x + 5y$.

The constraints are $x \leq 80$, $y \geq 60$, $x + y \leq 200$, $x \geq 0$, and $y \geq 0$.

The feasible region is a polygon bounded by the vertices $(0, 60)$, $(80, 60)$, $(80, 120)$, and $(0, 200)$.

Evaluating the objective function $z$ at each of these corner points:
At $(0, 60)$, $z = 3(0) + 5(60) = 300$
At $(80, 60)$, $z = 3(80) + 5(60) = 240 + 300 = 540$
At $(80, 120)$, $z = 3(80) + 5(120) = 240 + 600 = 840$
At $(0, 200)$, $z = 3(0) + 5(200) = 1000$

The minimum value of $z$ is $300$, which occurs at the point $(0, 60)$.

Answer: $(0, 60)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The negation of the contrapositive of the statement $(p \vee \sim q) \to (p \wedge \sim q)$ is
questions.solution:
The contrapositive of a conditional statement $X \to Y$ is logically equivalent to the statement itself.

Therefore, the negation of the contrapositive of $X \to Y$ is logically equivalent to the negation of $X \to Y$.

The negation of $X \to Y$ is $X \wedge \sim Y$.

Given the statement $(p \vee \sim q) \to (p \wedge \sim q)$, we have $X = p \vee \sim q$ and $Y = p \wedge \sim q$.

The negation of the statement is:

$X \wedge \sim Y = (p \vee \sim q) \wedge \sim (p \wedge \sim q)$

By De Morgan's laws, $\sim (p \wedge \sim q) \equiv \sim p \vee q$.

Substituting this back, we get:

$(p \vee \sim q) \wedge (\sim p \vee q)$

Rearranging the terms, this is identical to $(\sim p \vee q) \wedge (p \vee \sim q)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the truth value of the compound statement $[(p \leftrightarrow q) \wedge (q \to r) \wedge \sim r] \to (p \wedge \sim q)$ is false, then the truth values of the statement patterns $(p \to q) \leftrightarrow (q \to r)$ and $\sim(p \vee r) \to (q \wedge p)$ are, respectively ...
questions.solution:
The given compound statement is $[(p \leftrightarrow q) \wedge (q \to r) \wedge \sim r] \to (p \wedge \sim q)$.

An implication $X \to Y$ is false if and only if $X$ is true and $Y$ is false.

Thus, $(p \leftrightarrow q) \wedge (q \to r) \wedge \sim r$ is true and $p \wedge \sim q$ is false.

For the conjunction $(p \leftrightarrow q) \wedge (q \to r) \wedge \sim r$ to be true, each of its components must be true:
$\sim r$ is true $\Rightarrow r = F$
$q \to r$ is true $\Rightarrow q \to F$ is true $\Rightarrow q = F$
$p \leftrightarrow q$ is true $\Rightarrow p \leftrightarrow F$ is true $\Rightarrow p = F$

Checking the second part with these values: $p \wedge \sim q = F \wedge T = F$, which satisfies the condition that $Y$ is false.

So, the truth values are $p = F$, $q = F$, $r = F$.

Now, evaluating the first statement pattern:
$(p \to q) \leftrightarrow (q \to r)$
$= (F \to F) \leftrightarrow (F \to F)$
$= T \leftrightarrow T = T$

Evaluating the second statement pattern:
$\sim(p \vee r) \to (q \wedge p)$
$= \sim(F \vee F) \to (F \wedge F)$
$= \sim F \to F$
$= T \to F = F$

The truth values are $T$ and $F$, respectively.

Answer: $(T, F)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $A^2 + xA + yI_2 = O_2$, where $I_2$ and $O_2$ are the identity matrix and null matrix of order 2 respectively, then:
questions.solution:
$A^2 = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$

Substituting $A^2$, $A$, and $I_2$ into the given equation $A^2 + xA + yI_2 = O_2$:

$\begin{bmatrix} 4 & -4 \\ 0 & 4 \end{bmatrix} + x \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 \end{bmatrix} + y \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$

$\begin{bmatrix} 4 + 2x + y & -4 - x \\ 0 & 4 + 2x + y \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 \end{bmatrix}$

Equating the corresponding elements to zero:

$-4 - x = 0 \Rightarrow x = -4$

$4 + 2x + y = 0$

Substituting $x = -4$ into the second equation:

$4 + 2(-4) + y = 0 \Rightarrow y = 4$

Answer: $x = -4,\ y = 4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A = [a_{ij}]_{3 \times 3}$ is a matrix such that $a_{ij} = |2i - 5j|$, where $|.|$ denotes the modulus function, then the element in the $2^{\text{nd}}$ row and $3^{\text{rd}}$ column of $A^{-1}$ is ...
questions.solution:
Given $a_{ij} = |2i - 5j|$, we construct the matrix $A$ of order $3 \times 3$:

$A = \begin{bmatrix} |2(1)-5(1)| & |2(1)-5(2)| & |2(1)-5(3)| \\ |2(2)-5(1)| & |2(2)-5(2)| & |2(2)-5(3)| \\ |2(3)-5(1)| & |2(3)-5(2)| & |2(3)-5(3)| \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 & 8 & 13 \\ 1 & 6 & 11 \\ 1 & 4 & 9 \end{bmatrix}$

The determinant of matrix $A$ is:

$|A| = 3(54 - 44) - 8(9 - 11) + 13(4 - 6)$

$|A| = 3(10) - 8(-2) + 13(-2) = 30 + 16 - 26 = 20$

The element in the $2^{\text{nd}}$ row and $3^{\text{rd}}$ column of $A^{-1}$ is given by $\dfrac{C_{32}}{|A|}$, where $C_{32}$ is the cofactor of the element $a_{32}$ in matrix $A$.

Calculating the cofactor $C_{32}$:

$C_{32} = (-1)^{3+2} \begin{vmatrix} 3 & 13 \\ 1 & 11 \end{vmatrix} = -(33 - 13) = -20$

Therefore, the required element is:

$\dfrac{C_{32}}{|A|} = \dfrac{-20}{20} = -1$

Answer: $-1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 5 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$, $B^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{1}{5} & \dfrac{2}{5} \\ \dfrac{2}{5} & -\dfrac{1}{5} \end{bmatrix}$, then $(AB)^{-1} = $
questions.solution:
Using the reversal law for the inverse of a product of matrices, we have:

$(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1}$

First, we find the inverse of matrix $A$. The determinant of $A$ is:

$|A| = (2)(-2) - (3)(5) = -4 - 15 = -19$

The adjugate of $A$ is obtained by swapping the diagonal elements and changing the signs of the off-diagonal elements:

$\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} -2 & -3 \\ -5 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$

Thus, $A^{-1}$ is given by:

$A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|} \text{adj}(A) = \dfrac{1}{-19} \begin{bmatrix} -2 & -3 \\ -5 & 2 \end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{19} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 5 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$

We are given $B^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} \dfrac{1}{5} & \dfrac{2}{5} \\ \dfrac{2}{5} & -\dfrac{1}{5} \end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{5} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix}$.

Now, we compute $(AB)^{-1}$ by multiplying $B^{-1}$ and $A^{-1}$:

$(AB)^{-1} = B^{-1}A^{-1} = \left( \dfrac{1}{5} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix} \right) \left( \dfrac{1}{19} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 5 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \right)$

$(AB)^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{95} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 \\ 5 & -2 \end{bmatrix}$

Performing the matrix multiplication:

$(AB)^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{95} \begin{bmatrix} (1)(2) + (2)(5) & (1)(3) + (2)(-2) \\ (2)(2) + (-1)(5) & (2)(3) + (-1)(-2) \end{bmatrix}$

$(AB)^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{95} \begin{bmatrix} 2 + 10 & 3 - 4 \\ 4 - 5 & 6 + 2 \end{bmatrix} = \dfrac{1}{95} \begin{bmatrix} 12 & -1 \\ -1 & 8 \end{bmatrix}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{95}\begin{bmatrix} 12 & -1 \\ -1 & 8 \end{bmatrix}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The combined equation of the pair of lines passing through the origin and making an angle $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ with the line $3x + y - 6 = 0$ is...
questions.solution:
Slope of the given line $3x + y - 6 = 0$ is $m_1 = -3$.

Let $m$ be the slope of the required line. Since the angle between the lines is $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$, we have:

$\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \left| \dfrac{m - m_1}{1 + m m_1} \right|$

$1 = \left| \dfrac{m - (-3)}{1 + m(-3)} \right| = \left| \dfrac{m + 3}{1 - 3m} \right|$

This gives two cases:

$\dfrac{m + 3}{1 - 3m} = 1 \Rightarrow m + 3 = 1 - 3m \Rightarrow 4m = -2 \Rightarrow m = -\dfrac{1}{2}$

$\dfrac{m + 3}{1 - 3m} = -1 \Rightarrow m + 3 = -1 + 3m \Rightarrow 2m = 4 \Rightarrow m = 2$

The equations of the lines passing through the origin with these slopes are $y = -\dfrac{1}{2}x$ and $y = 2x$, which can be written as $x + 2y = 0$ and $2x - y = 0$.

The combined equation of the pair of lines is:

$(x + 2y)(2x - y) = 0$

$2x^2 - xy + 4xy - 2y^2 = 0$

$2x^2 + 3xy - 2y^2 = 0$

Answer: $2x^2 + 3xy - 2y^2 = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\theta$ is the acute angle between the lines $2x^2 + 7xy + 3y^2 = 0$, then the value of $\dfrac{2\cos\theta - 3\sin\theta}{4\sin\theta + 5\cos\theta} = \ldots$
questions.solution:
Given equation of the pair of straight lines is $2x^2 + 7xy + 3y^2 = 0$.

Comparing with $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0$, we get $a = 2$, $h = \dfrac{7}{2}$, and $b = 3$.

The acute angle $\theta$ between the lines is given by:

$\tan\theta = \left| \dfrac{2\sqrt{h^2 - ab}}{a + b} \right|$

$\tan\theta = \left| \dfrac{2\sqrt{\left(\dfrac{7}{2}\right)^2 - (2)(3)}}{2 + 3} \right|$

$\tan\theta = \left| \dfrac{2\sqrt{\dfrac{49}{4} - 6}}{5} \right| = \left| \dfrac{2\sqrt{\dfrac{25}{4}}}{5} \right| = \dfrac{2 \times \dfrac{5}{2}}{5} = 1$

We need to find the value of $\dfrac{2\cos\theta - 3\sin\theta}{4\sin\theta + 5\cos\theta}$.

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $\cos\theta$, we get:

$\dfrac{2 - 3\tan\theta}{4\tan\theta + 5}$

Substituting $\tan\theta = 1$:

$\dfrac{2 - 3(1)}{4(1) + 5} = \dfrac{-1}{9} = -\dfrac{1}{9}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{1}{9}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The number of 4-letter words formed from the English alphabet such that there are exactly 2 vowels and 2 consonants and no vowel is repeated, but consonants may be repeated is:
questions.solution:
The 4-letter word requires exactly 2 vowels and 2 consonants.

The number of ways to choose 2 positions out of 4 for the vowels is $^{4}C_{2}$.

Since no vowel is repeated, the number of ways to choose and arrange 2 distinct vowels from the 5 available vowels in the chosen positions is $^{5}P_{2}$.

The remaining 2 positions must be filled with consonants. Since there are 21 consonants and repetition is allowed, each position can be filled in 21 ways. The number of ways to fill the consonant positions is $21 \times 21 = (21)^2$.

The total number of 4-letter words formed is $^{4}C_{2} \times ^{5}P_{2} \times (21)^2$.

Answer: ${}^{4}C_2 \times {}^{5}P_2 \times (21)^2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $E_1$ and $E_2$ are equally likely, mutually exclusive and exhaustive events and $P(A|E_1) = 0.2$, $P(A|E_2) = 0.3$, then $P(E_1|A)$ equal to...
questions.solution:
Since $E_1$ and $E_2$ are equally likely, mutually exclusive and exhaustive events, $P(E_1) = P(E_2) = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Given $P(A|E_1) = 0.2$ and $P(A|E_2) = 0.3$.

Using Bayes' theorem,

$P(E_1|A) = \dfrac{P(A|E_1)P(E_1)}{P(A|E_1)P(E_1) + P(A|E_2)P(E_2)}$

$P(E_1|A) = \dfrac{0.2 \times \dfrac{1}{2}}{0.2 \times \dfrac{1}{2} + 0.3 \times \dfrac{1}{2}}$

$P(E_1|A) = \dfrac{0.2}{0.2 + 0.3} = \dfrac{0.2}{0.5} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a random variable $X$ has a probability mass function $P(x) = \begin{cases} kx^2, & \text{for } x = 1, 2, 3, 4 \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}$, then the mean of $X$ is ...
questions.solution:
The sum of all probabilities must be equal to $1$.

$\sum_{x=1}^{4} P(x) = 1$

$k(1^2 + 2^2 + 3^2 + 4^2) = 1$

$k(1 + 4 + 9 + 16) = 1$

$30k = 1 \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{1}{30}$

The mean of the random variable $X$ is given by $E(X) = \sum_{x=1}^{4} x P(x)$.

$E(X) = \sum_{x=1}^{4} x(kx^2) = k \sum_{x=1}^{4} x^3$

$E(X) = \dfrac{1}{30} (1^3 + 2^3 + 3^3 + 4^3)$

$E(X) = \dfrac{1}{30} (1 + 8 + 27 + 64)$

$E(X) = \dfrac{100}{30} = \dfrac{10}{3} = 3.333$

Answer: $3.333$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If a fair coin is tossed 8 times, then the probability of getting at most 2 heads is...
questions.solution:
Let $X$ be the number of heads obtained in $8$ tosses of a fair coin.

The probability of getting a head is $p = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and a tail is $q = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

The probability of getting exactly $r$ heads is given by $P(X = r) = ^{8}C_{r} \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^r \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{8-r} = \dfrac{^{8}C_{r}}{256}$.

The probability of getting at most $2$ heads is $P(X \le 2) = P(X = 0) + P(X = 1) + P(X = 2)$.

$P(X \le 2) = \dfrac{^{8}C_{0}}{256} + \dfrac{^{8}C_{1}}{256} + \dfrac{^{8}C_{2}}{256}$

$P(X \le 2) = \dfrac{1 + 8 + 28}{256} = \dfrac{37}{256}$

Answer: $\dfrac{37}{256}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In triangle ABC, with usual notations, if $a = 4, b = 5$ and $c = 6$, then angle C is equal to...
questions.solution:
Using the cosine rule:

$\cos A = \dfrac{b^2 + c^2 - a^2}{2bc}$

$\cos A = \dfrac{5^2 + 6^2 - 4^2}{2(5)(6)} = \dfrac{25 + 36 - 16}{60} = \dfrac{45}{60} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Similarly, for angle C:

$\cos C = \dfrac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab}$

$\cos C = \dfrac{4^2 + 5^2 - 6^2}{2(4)(5)} = \dfrac{16 + 25 - 36}{40} = \dfrac{5}{40} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

Using the double angle formula:

$\cos 2A = 2\cos^2 A - 1$

$\cos 2A = 2\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^2 - 1 = 2\left(\dfrac{9}{16}\right) - 1 = \dfrac{9}{8} - 1 = \dfrac{1}{8}$

Since $\cos C = \cos 2A$ and both angles lie in $(0, \pi)$, we get $C = 2A$.

Answer: $2A$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The line $(2 + k)x + (1 + k)y = 5 + 7k$ passes through the fixed point for different values of k. If 'd' is the distance of a fixed point from the origin, then $d^2 = \ldots$
questions.solution:
The given equation of the line is $(2 + k)x + (1 + k)y = 5 + 7k$.

Rearranging the terms to express it in the form $L_1 + kL_2 = 0$:

$2x + kx + y + ky - 5 - 7k = 0$

$(2x + y - 5) + k(x + y - 7) = 0$

This represents a family of lines passing through the point of intersection of the lines:

$2x + y - 5 = 0$

$x + y - 7 = 0$

Solving these two equations simultaneously, we subtract the second equation from the first:

$(2x + y - 5) - (x + y - 7) = 0$

$x + 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = -2$

Substituting $x = -2$ into the second equation:

$-2 + y - 7 = 0 \Rightarrow y = 9$

The fixed point is $(-2, 9)$.

The distance $d$ of this fixed point from the origin $(0, 0)$ is given by:

$d^2 = (-2 - 0)^2 + (9 - 0)^2$

$d^2 = 4 + 81 = 85$

Answer: $85$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The values of p and q so that the line joining the points (7, p, 2) and (q, -2, 5) may be parallel to the line joining the points (2, -3, 5) and (-6, -15, 11) are
questions.solution:
The direction ratios of the line joining the points $(7, p, 2)$ and $(q, -2, 5)$ are $(q - 7, -2 - p, 5 - 2) = (q - 7, -2 - p, 3)$.

The direction ratios of the line joining the points $(2, -3, 5)$ and $(-6, -15, 11)$ are $(-6 - 2, -15 - (-3), 11 - 5) = (-8, -12, 6)$.

Since the two lines are parallel, their direction ratios are proportional:

$\dfrac{q - 7}{-8} = \dfrac{-2 - p}{-12} = \dfrac{3}{6}$

$\dfrac{q - 7}{-8} = \dfrac{-2 - p}{-12} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Equating the terms to $\dfrac{1}{2}$:

$\dfrac{q - 7}{-8} = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow q - 7 = -4 \Rightarrow q = 3$

$\dfrac{-2 - p}{-12} = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow -2 - p = -6 \Rightarrow p = 4$

Therefore, $p = 4$ and $q = 3$.

Answer: $p = 4,\ q = 3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $d$ is the distance of point (2, 5, 10) from the plane containing the lines $\bar{r} = (4\hat{j} - \hat{k}) + \lambda(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$ and $\bar{r} = (2\hat{i} + \hat{j}) + \mu(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$, then $d^2 = $
questions.solution:
The given lines are:
$\bar{r} = (4\hat{j} - \hat{k}) + \lambda(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$
$\bar{r} = (2\hat{i} + \hat{j}) + \mu(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k})$

The lines are parallel with direction vector $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 2\hat{k}$.
Let $A(0, 4, -1)$ be a point on the first line and $B(2, 1, 0)$ be a point on the second line.
The vector joining $A$ and $B$ is $\vec{AB} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}$.

The normal vector $\vec{n}$ to the plane containing these two lines is perpendicular to both $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{AB}$:
$\vec{n} = \vec{b} \times \vec{AB} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 1 & 2 & -2 \\ 2 & -3 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$
$\vec{n} = \hat{i}(2 - 6) - \hat{j}(1 - (-4)) + \hat{k}(-3 - 4) = -4\hat{i} - 5\hat{j} - 7\hat{k}$

Taking the normal vector as $4\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$, the equation of the plane passing through $A(0, 4, -1)$ is:
$4(x - 0) + 5(y - 4) + 7(z + 1) = 0$
$4x + 5y + 7z - 13 = 0$

The perpendicular distance $d$ of the point $P(2, 5, 10)$ from this plane is:
$d = \dfrac{|4(2) + 5(5) + 7(10) - 13|}{\sqrt{4^2 + 5^2 + 7^2}}$
$d = \dfrac{|8 + 25 + 70 - 13|}{\sqrt{16 + 25 + 49}}$
$d = \dfrac{90}{\sqrt{90}} = \sqrt{90}$

Therefore, $d^2 = 90$.

Answer: $90$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The vector equation of plane in parametric form, passing through the points (-1, 2, 0), (2, 2, -1) and parallel to the line $\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{2y+1}{2} = \dfrac{z+1}{-1}$ is
questions.solution:
The position vector of the point $A(-1, 2, 0)$ is $\vec{a} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}$.

The plane passes through $A(-1, 2, 0)$ and $B(2, 2, -1)$. A vector parallel to the plane is $\vec{AB} = (2 - (-1))\hat{i} + (2 - 2)\hat{j} + (-1 - 0)\hat{k} = 3\hat{i} - \hat{k}$.

The given line is $\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{2y+1}{2} = \dfrac{z+1}{-1}$. Rewriting it in standard form, we get $\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{y+1/2}{1} = \dfrac{z+1}{-1}$.

The direction vector of the line is $\vec{v} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$. Since the plane is parallel to this line, $\vec{v}$ is also parallel to the plane.

The parametric vector equation of a plane passing through a point with position vector $\vec{a}$ and parallel to two non-collinear vectors $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{c}$ is given by $\vec{r} = \vec{a} + \lambda\vec{b} + \mu\vec{c}$.

Substituting $\vec{a} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}$, $\vec{b} = \vec{AB} = 3\hat{i} - \hat{k}$, and $\vec{c} = \vec{v} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$, we get:

$\vec{r} = (-\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}) + \lambda(3\hat{i} - \hat{k}) + \mu(\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k})$

Answer: $\bar{r} = (-\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}) + \lambda(3\hat{i} - \hat{k}) + \mu(\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k})$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the lines $2x = ky = -z$ and $6x = -y = -4z$ are perpendicular to each other then the value of $k$ is ...
questions.solution:
The equations of the given lines can be rewritten in standard symmetric form as:

$\dfrac{x}{1/2} = \dfrac{y}{1/k} = \dfrac{z}{-1}$

$\dfrac{x}{1/6} = \dfrac{y}{-1} = \dfrac{z}{-1/4}$

The direction ratios of the first line are $a_1 = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $b_1 = \dfrac{1}{k}$, $c_1 = -1$.

The direction ratios of the second line are $a_2 = \dfrac{1}{6}$, $b_2 = -1$, $c_2 = -\dfrac{1}{4}$.

Since the two lines are perpendicular to each other, the sum of the products of their corresponding direction ratios must be zero:

$a_1 a_2 + b_1 b_2 + c_1 c_2 = 0$

$\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{6}\right) + \left(\dfrac{1}{k}\right)(-1) + (-1)\left(-\dfrac{1}{4}\right) = 0$

$\dfrac{1}{12} - \dfrac{1}{k} + \dfrac{1}{4} = 0$

$\dfrac{1}{k} = \dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{3}{12}$

$\dfrac{1}{k} = \dfrac{4}{12}$

$\dfrac{1}{k} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$k = 3$

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The general solution of the equation $\cot\theta \cdot \cot 2\theta = 1$ is...
questions.solution:
Given equation is $\cot\theta \cdot \cot 2\theta = 1$

Writing in terms of $\tan\theta$:

$\dfrac{1}{\tan\theta} \cdot \dfrac{1 - \tan^2\theta}{2\tan\theta} = 1$

$1 - \tan^2\theta = 2\tan^2\theta$

$3\tan^2\theta = 1$

$\tan^2\theta = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$\tan^2\theta = \tan^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$

Using the general solution for $\tan^2\theta = \tan^2\alpha$, which is $\theta = n\pi \pm \alpha, n \in Z$, we get:

$\theta = n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{6}, n \in Z$

Answer: $\theta = n\pi \pm \dfrac{\pi}{6}, n \in Z$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\cos(60^\circ - A)\cdot\cos A\cdot\cos(60^\circ + A)$ is
questions.solution:
Using the identity $\cos(x - y)\cos(x + y) = \cos^2 x - \sin^2 y$

$\cos(60^\circ - A)\cos(60^\circ + A) = \cos^2 60^\circ - \sin^2 A$

$= \dfrac{1}{4} - \sin^2 A$

Multiplying by $\cos A$

$\cos A \left( \dfrac{1}{4} - \sin^2 A \right) = \dfrac{1}{4} \cos A - \cos A (1 - \cos^2 A)$

$= \cos^3 A - \dfrac{3}{4} \cos A$

$= \dfrac{4\cos^3 A - 3\cos A}{4}$

$= \dfrac{1}{4} \cos 3A$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{4}\cos 3A$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The volume of a parallelopiped with coterminous edges $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ is 3 cubic units. The volume (in cubic units) of a tetrahedron with coterminous edges $(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}), (\bar{a} \times 2\bar{c}), (\bar{b} \times 2\bar{c})$ is...
questions.solution:
The volume of the parallelopiped with coterminous edges $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ is given by $|[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}]| = 3$.

The volume of a tetrahedron with coterminous edges $\bar{x}, \bar{y}, \bar{z}$ is $V = \dfrac{1}{6} |[\bar{x} \bar{y} \bar{z}]|$.

Here, the edges are $\bar{x} = \bar{a} \times \bar{b}$, $\bar{y} = 2(\bar{a} \times \bar{c})$, and $\bar{z} = 2(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})$.

Evaluating the scalar triple product of these edges:
