$[\bar{x} \bar{y} \bar{z}] = [\bar{a} \times \bar{b} \quad 2(\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) \quad 2(\bar{b} \times \bar{c})] = 4 [\bar{a} \times \bar{b} \quad \bar{a} \times \bar{c} \quad \bar{b} \times \bar{c}]$

Using the scalar triple product expansion:

$[\bar{a} \times \bar{b} \quad \bar{a} \times \bar{c} \quad \bar{b} \times \bar{c}] = (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot ((\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}))$

Applying the vector triple product formula:

$(\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = [\bar{a} \bar{c} \bar{c}] \bar{b} - [\bar{a} \bar{c} \bar{b}] \bar{c}$

Since $[\bar{a} \bar{c} \bar{c}] = 0$ and $[\bar{a} \bar{c} \bar{b}] = -[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}]$, we get:

$(\bar{a} \times \bar{c}) \times (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = [\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}] \bar{c}$

Substituting this back into the scalar triple product:

$(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot ([\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}] \bar{c}) = [\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}] ((\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{c}) = [\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}]^2$

Therefore, the scalar triple product of the new edges is:

$[\bar{x} \bar{y} \bar{z}] = 4 [\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}]^2$

Since $|[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}]| = 3$, we have $[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}]^2 = 9$.

$[\bar{x} \bar{y} \bar{z}] = 4 \times 9 = 36$

The volume of the tetrahedron is $V = \dfrac{1}{6} \times 36 = 6$ cubic units.

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $\bar{a}, \bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$ be three coplanar unit vectors. A unit vector $\bar{d}$ is perpendicular to them. If $(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times (\bar{c} \times \bar{d}) = \dfrac{3}{26}\hat{i} - \dfrac{2}{13}\hat{j} + \dfrac{6}{13}\hat{k}$ and the angle between $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ is $30^\circ$, then $\bar{c}$ is equal to...
questions.solution:
Using the vector quadruple product expansion:

$(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \times (\bar{c} \times \bar{d}) = [\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{d}]\bar{c} - [\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}]\bar{d}$

Since $\bar{a}, \bar{b}, \bar{c}$ are coplanar, their scalar triple product $[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{c}] = 0$.

Thus, the expression simplifies to $[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{d}]\bar{c}$.

The scalar triple product is $[\bar{a} \bar{b} \bar{d}] = (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{d}$.

Since $\bar{d}$ is perpendicular to the coplanar vectors $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$, the vector $\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$ is parallel to $\bar{d}$.

The magnitude of $\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$ is given by $|\bar{a}| |\bar{b}| \sin 30^\circ = 1 \times 1 \times \dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Since $\bar{d}$ is a unit vector, $(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{d} = \pm |\bar{a} \times \bar{b}| |\bar{d}| = \pm \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Therefore, $\pm \dfrac{1}{2} \bar{c} = \dfrac{3}{26}\hat{i} - \dfrac{2}{13}\hat{j} + \dfrac{6}{13}\hat{k}$.

Multiplying by $\pm 2$ yields:

$\bar{c} = \pm \left( \dfrac{3}{13}\hat{i} - \dfrac{4}{13}\hat{j} + \dfrac{12}{13}\hat{k} \right)$

Taking the positive sign gives the matching option.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{13}\hat{i} - \dfrac{4}{13}\hat{j} + \dfrac{12}{13}\hat{k}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\bar{a} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$, $\bar{b} = \hat{i} + 3\hat{k}$ and $\bar{c}$ is a unit vector, then the maximum value of the scalar triple product $[\bar{a}\ \bar{b}\ \bar{c}]$ is
questions.solution:
The scalar triple product is given by $[\bar{a}\ \bar{b}\ \bar{c}] = (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{c}$.

First, calculating the cross product $\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$:

$\bar{a} \times \bar{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 0 & 3 \end{vmatrix}$

$= \hat{i}(3 - 0) - \hat{j}(6 - (-1)) + \hat{k}(0 - 1)$

$= 3\hat{i} - 7\hat{j} - \hat{k}$

The scalar triple product becomes $(3\hat{i} - 7\hat{j} - \hat{k}) \cdot \bar{c}$.

Using the dot product formula, $(\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot \bar{c} = |\bar{a} \times \bar{b}| |\bar{c}| \cos \theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$ and $\bar{c}$.

Since $\bar{c}$ is a unit vector, $|\bar{c}| = 1$. The maximum value occurs when $\cos \theta = 1$ (i.e., when $\bar{c}$ is parallel to $\bar{a} \times \bar{b}$).

Maximum value $= |\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|$

$= \sqrt{3^2 + (-7)^2 + (-1)^2}$

$= \sqrt{9 + 49 + 1} = \sqrt{59}$

Answer: $\sqrt{59}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $\bar{a} = 4\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\bar{b} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\bar{c} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$, then $(\bar{a} + \bar{b}) \cdot (\bar{b} + \bar{c}) = $
questions.solution:
Given vectors are $\bar{a} = 4\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\bar{b} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$ and $\bar{c} = 3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j} + 5\hat{k}$.

Calculating $\bar{a} + \bar{b}$:

$\bar{a} + \bar{b} = (4+2)\hat{i} + (1+1)\hat{j} + (1+2)\hat{k} = 6\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$

Calculating $\bar{b} + \bar{c}$:

$\bar{b} + \bar{c} = (2+3)\hat{i} + (1+4)\hat{j} + (2+5)\hat{k} = 5\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$

Taking the dot product:

$(\bar{a} + \bar{b}) \cdot (\bar{b} + \bar{c}) = (6\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}) \cdot (5\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 7\hat{k})$

$= (6 \times 5) + (2 \times 5) + (3 \times 7)$

$= 30 + 10 + 21 = 61$

Answer: $61$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of a line in cartesian form passing through (0, 0, 0) and (4, 3, c) and parallel to $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$ where $\vec{a} = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = 3\hat{i} - 4\hat{j}$ is
questions.solution:
The direction vector of the line is parallel to $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$.

$\vec{a} \times \vec{b} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & -4 & 0 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(0 - (-8)) - \hat{j}(0 - 6) + \hat{k}(-8 - 3) = 8\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} - 11\hat{k}$

The direction ratios of the line are proportional to $8, 6, -11$.

The line passes through $(0, 0, 0)$ and $(4, 3, c)$. Its direction ratios are $4 - 0, 3 - 0, c - 0$, which is $4, 3, c$.

Since the line is parallel to $\vec{a} \times \vec{b}$, the direction ratios must be proportional:

$\dfrac{4}{8} = \dfrac{3}{6} = \dfrac{c}{-11}$

$\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{c}{-11} \Rightarrow c = -\dfrac{11}{2}$

The line passes through the point $(4, 3, c) = \left(4, 3, -\dfrac{11}{2}\right)$.

The equation of the line in Cartesian form is:

$\dfrac{x - 4}{8} = \dfrac{y - 3}{6} = \dfrac{z - \left(-\dfrac{11}{2}\right)}{-11}$

$\dfrac{x - 4}{8} = \dfrac{y - 3}{6} = \dfrac{z + \dfrac{11}{2}}{-11}$

Answer: $\dfrac{x-4}{8} = \dfrac{y-3}{6} = \dfrac{z + \frac{11}{2}}{-11}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An inductor of inductance $2\ \mu\text{H}$ is connected in series with a resistance, a variable capacitor and an a.c. source of 10 kHz. The value of capacitance for which maximum current is drawn in to the circuit is $\dfrac{1}{x}\ \text{F}$, where the value of x is (Take $\pi^2 = 10$)
questions.solution:
Maximum current is drawn in a series LCR circuit at resonance.

At resonance, the inductive reactance equals the capacitive reactance, so $\omega L = \dfrac{1}{\omega C}$.

$C = \dfrac{1}{\omega^2 L} = \dfrac{1}{(2\pi f)^2 L}$

Given $L = 2\ \mu\text{H} = 2 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{H}$ and $f = 10\ \text{kHz} = 10^4\ \text{Hz}$.

$C = \dfrac{1}{4\pi^2 f^2 L}$

Substituting the values and using $\pi^2 = 10$:

$C = \dfrac{1}{4 \times 10 \times (10^4)^2 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}}$

$C = \dfrac{1}{40 \times 10^8 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}}$

$C = \dfrac{1}{80 \times 10^2} = \dfrac{1}{8000}\ \text{F}$

Comparing with $C = \dfrac{1}{x}\ \text{F}$, we get $x = 8000$.

Answer: $8000$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Series LCR circuit containing an a.c. source of 100V has a inductor and a capacitor of reactance $24\ \Omega$ and $16\ \Omega$ respectively. If a resistance of $6\ \Omega$ is connected in series, then the potential difference across the series combination of inductor and capacitor only is
questions.solution:
Given $V = 100\text{V}$, $X_L = 24\ \Omega$, $X_C = 16\ \Omega$, and $R = 6\ \Omega$.

The net reactance of the circuit is $X = X_L - X_C = 24 - 16 = 8\ \Omega$.

The impedance of the series LCR circuit is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$.

Substituting the values, $Z = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{36 + 64} = 10\ \Omega$.

The rms current in the circuit is $I = \dfrac{V}{Z} = \dfrac{100}{10} = 10\text{A}$.

The potential difference across the series combination of the inductor and capacitor is $V_{LC} = I \times |X_L - X_C|$.

$V_{LC} = 10 \times 8 = 80\text{V}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Alternating current of peak value $\left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right)$ A flows through the primary coil of a transformer. The coefficient of mutual inductance between primary and secondary coils is 1H. The peak value of induced e.m.f. in the secondary coil is
(Frequency of a.c. = 50 Hz)
questions.solution:
The current in the primary coil is $I = I_0 \sin(\omega t)$.

The induced e.m.f. in the secondary coil is given by $e = -M \dfrac{dI}{dt}$.

$e = -M \dfrac{d}{dt} (I_0 \sin(\omega t)) = -M I_0 \omega \cos(\omega t)$

The peak value of the induced e.m.f. is $e_0 = M I_0 \omega$.

Given $M = 1$ H, $I_0 = \dfrac{2}{\pi}$ A, and $f = 50$ Hz.

The angular frequency is $\omega = 2\pi f = 2\pi \times 50 = 100\pi$ rad/s.

Substituting the values, we get:

$e_0 = 1 \times \left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right) \times 100\pi = 200$ V.

Answer: $200\text{V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
An electron makes a transition from an excited state to the ground state of a hydrogen like atom. Out of the following statements which one is correct ?
(A) K.E, P. E. and T.E. decreases
(B) K.E. increases but P. E. and T.E. decreases
(C) K.E. and T.E. decreases but P.E. increases
(D) K.E. decreases, P.E. increases but T.E. remains the same
questions.solution:
For a hydrogen-like atom, the kinetic energy, potential energy, and total energy of an electron in the $n$-th orbit are given by:

$K.E. = \dfrac{13.6 Z^2}{n^2} \text{ eV}$

$P.E. = -\dfrac{27.2 Z^2}{n^2} \text{ eV}$

$T.E. = -\dfrac{13.6 Z^2}{n^2} \text{ eV}$

When the electron makes a transition from an excited state to the ground state, the principal quantum number $n$ decreases.

As $n$ decreases, $\dfrac{1}{n^2}$ increases.

Therefore, $K.E.$ increases.

Since $P.E.$ and $T.E.$ are negative, their magnitudes increase, which means their actual values decrease (become more negative).

Thus, K.E. increases but P.E. and T.E. decrease.

Answer: B

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A capacitor has capacity C when it's parallel plates are separated by air medium of thickness 'd'. A slab of material of dielectric constant K having area equal to that of plates but thickness $\dfrac{d}{2}$ is inserted between the plates. Capacitance of the capacitor in the presence of slab will be
questions.solution:
Initial capacitance of the parallel plate capacitor with air is given by

$C = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{d}$

When a dielectric slab of thickness $t = \dfrac{d}{2}$ and dielectric constant $K$ is inserted, the system can be considered as two capacitors in series.

Capacitance of the air-filled part of thickness $\dfrac{d}{2}$ is

$C_1 = \dfrac{\epsilon_0 A}{\dfrac{d}{2}} = \dfrac{2\epsilon_0 A}{d} = 2C$

Capacitance of the dielectric-filled part of thickness $\dfrac{d}{2}$ is

$C_2 = \dfrac{K\epsilon_0 A}{\dfrac{d}{2}} = \dfrac{2K\epsilon_0 A}{d} = 2KC$

The equivalent capacitance $C'$ of these two capacitors in series is

$C' = \dfrac{C_1 C_2}{C_1 + C_2}$

Substituting the values of $C_1$ and $C_2$:

$C' = \dfrac{(2C)(2KC)}{2C + 2KC}$

$C' = \dfrac{4KC^2}{2C(K + 1)}$

$C' = \dfrac{2KC}{K + 1}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2\text{KC}}{\text{K}+1}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the potential difference between points B and D is zero in the given circuit, the value of x is $\dfrac{1}{n}\ \Omega$. The value n is
questions.solution:
The given circuit is a Wheatstone bridge. Since the potential difference between points B and D is zero, the bridge is balanced.

Let the nodes be A (left), B (top), C (right), and D (bottom).

The equivalent resistance of the arm AB is:
$R_{AB} = \dfrac{6 \times 3}{6 + 3} = \dfrac{18}{9} = 2\ \Omega$

The equivalent resistance of the arm AD is:
$R_{AD} = 1 + 2 = 3\ \Omega$

The equivalent resistance of the arm BC is:
$R_{BC} = \dfrac{x \times 1}{x + 1} = \dfrac{x}{x + 1}\ \Omega$

The equivalent resistance of the arm DC is:
$R_{DC} = x\ \Omega$

For a balanced Wheatstone bridge, the condition is:
$\dfrac{R_{AB}}{R_{AD}} = \dfrac{R_{BC}}{R_{DC}}$

Substituting the values:
$\dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{\dfrac{x}{x + 1}}{x}$

$\dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{1}{x + 1}$

$2(x + 1) = 3$

$2x + 2 = 3$

$2x = 1$

$x = \dfrac{1}{2}\ \Omega$

Given $x = \dfrac{1}{n}\ \Omega$, we get $n = 2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A galvanometer has resistance G and range Vg. How much resistance is required to read voltage up to V volt?
questions.solution:
The current for full-scale deflection of the galvanometer is $I_g = \dfrac{V_g}{G}$.

To convert the galvanometer into a voltmeter of range $V$, a high resistance $R$ is connected in series with it.

The total resistance of the circuit becomes $G + R$.

The new voltage range is given by $V = I_g(G + R)$.

Substituting $I_g = \dfrac{V_g}{G}$ into the equation:

$V = \dfrac{V_g}{G}(G + R)$

$\dfrac{V}{V_g} = \dfrac{G + R}{G}$

$\dfrac{V}{V_g} = 1 + \dfrac{R}{G}$

$\dfrac{R}{G} = \dfrac{V}{V_g} - 1$

$R = G\left(\dfrac{V}{V_g} - 1\right)$

Answer: $G\left(\dfrac{V}{V_g} - 1\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A photoemissive substance is illuminated with a radiation of wavelength $\lambda_i$ so that it releases electrons with de-Broglie wavelength $\lambda_e$. The longest wavelength of radiation that can emit photoelectron is $\lambda_0$. Expression for de-Broglie wavelength is (m = mass of electron, h = Planck's constant, C = Speed of light)
questions.solution:
Using Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectron is given by:

$K_{\text{max}} = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_i} - \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_0} = hc \left( \dfrac{1}{\lambda_i} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_0} \right)$

The de-Broglie wavelength of the emitted electron is:

$\lambda_e = \dfrac{h}{p} = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK_{\text{max}}}}$

Substituting the value of $K_{\text{max}}$:

$\lambda_e = \dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mhc \left( \dfrac{1}{\lambda_i} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_0} \right)}}$

$\lambda_e = \sqrt{\dfrac{h^2}{2mhc \left( \dfrac{1}{\lambda_i} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_0} \right)}}$

$\lambda_e = \left[ \dfrac{h}{2mc \left( \dfrac{1}{\lambda_i} - \dfrac{1}{\lambda_0} \right)} \right]^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a light of wavelength '$\lambda$' falls on the emitter of a photosensitive surface, maximum speed of emitted photoelectrons is 'V'. If the incident wavelength is changed to '$2\lambda/3$', maximum speed of emitted photoelectrons will be
questions.solution:
According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is given by

$\dfrac{1}{2}mV^2 = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi$

When the incident wavelength is changed to $\dfrac{2\lambda}{3}$, the new maximum kinetic energy is

$\dfrac{1}{2}mV'^2 = \dfrac{hc}{\dfrac{2\lambda}{3}} - \phi = \dfrac{3hc}{2\lambda} - \phi$

Substituting $\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = \dfrac{1}{2}mV^2 + \phi$ into the above equation, we get

$\dfrac{1}{2}mV'^2 = \dfrac{3}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}mV^2 + \phi\right) - \phi$

$\dfrac{1}{2}mV'^2 = \dfrac{3}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}mV^2\right) + \dfrac{\phi}{2}$

Since the work function $\phi \gt 0$, it follows that

$\dfrac{1}{2}mV'^2 \gt \dfrac{3}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}mV^2\right)$

$V'^2 \gt 1.5 V^2$

$V' \gt V(1.5)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

Thus, the maximum speed of emitted photoelectrons will be greater than $V(1.5)^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the given circuit, if $dI/dt = -1\ \text{A/s}$ then the value of $V_{AB}$ at this instant will be
questions.solution:
Applying Kirchhoff's Voltage Law (KVL) from point A to point B:

$V_A - IR - L \dfrac{dI}{dt} - V_{\text{battery}} = V_B$

Given:
$I = 2\ \text{A}$
$R = 6\ \Omega$
$L = 3\ \text{H}$
$\dfrac{dI}{dt} = -1\ \text{A/s}$
$V_{\text{battery}} = 6\ \text{V}$ (Moving from left to right along the bottom wire, the path goes from the positive to the negative terminal, so it is a potential drop)

Substituting the values into the KVL equation:

$V_A - (2)(6) - (3)(-1) - 6 = V_B$

$V_A - 12 + 3 - 6 = V_B$

$V_A - 15 = V_B$

$V_{AB} = V_A - V_B = 15\ \text{V}$

Answer: $15\text{V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A graph of magnetic flux ($\Phi$) versus current (I) is shown for four inductors A, B, C, D. The smallest value of self inductance is for inductor.
questions.solution:
The magnetic flux $\Phi$ linked with an inductor is related to the current $I$ by the equation:

$\Phi = LI$

where $L$ is the self-inductance.

From the equation, it is clear that the graph of $\Phi$ versus $I$ is a straight line passing through the origin, and its slope is equal to the self-inductance $L$.

$\text{Slope} = \dfrac{\Phi}{I} = L$

To find the inductor with the smallest self-inductance, we need to identify the line with the minimum slope.

From the given graph, the slopes of the lines are in the order:

$\text{Slope}_A \gt \text{Slope}_B \gt \text{Slope}_C \gt \text{Slope}_D$

Therefore, $L_A \gt L_B \gt L_C \gt L_D$.

Inductor D has the smallest slope and hence the smallest value of self-inductance.

Answer: D

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular coil of radius 'r' is placed on another circular coil whose radius is 'R' and the current flowing through it is changing and their centers coincide. ($R \gg r$). If both the coils are coplanar, then the mutual inductance between them is proportional to
questions.solution:
Let the current in the larger coil of radius $R$ be $I$.

The magnetic field produced by the larger coil at its center is $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$.

Since $R \gg r$, the magnetic field can be considered uniform over the entire area of the smaller coil.

The magnetic flux linked with the smaller coil of radius $r$ is $\Phi = B A = \left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}\right) (\pi r^2)$.

The mutual inductance $M$ is given by $M = \dfrac{\Phi}{I} = \dfrac{\mu_0 \pi r^2}{2R}$.

Therefore, $M \propto \dfrac{r^2}{R}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{r^2}{R}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two charges $q_1$ and $q_2$ are separated by a distance of 30cm. A third charge $q_3$ initially at point C is shown in figure, is moved along the circular path of radius 40 cm from C to D. If the difference in potential energy due to movement of $q_3$ from C to D is $q_3 k/4\pi\varepsilon_0$, the value of K is ($\varepsilon_0$ = permittivity of free space)
questions.solution:
The initial potential energy of the system when charge $q_3$ is at point C is given by:

$U_C = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \left( \dfrac{q_1 q_3}{AC} + \dfrac{q_2 q_3}{BC} \right)$

From the given figure, $AC = 40\text{ cm} = 0.4\text{ m}$ and $AB = 30\text{ cm} = 0.3\text{ m}$.
In the right-angled triangle ABC, the distance BC is:
$BC = \sqrt{AB^2 + AC^2} = \sqrt{(0.3)^2 + (0.4)^2} = 0.5\text{ m}$

So, $U_C = \dfrac{q_3}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \left( \dfrac{q_1}{0.4} + \dfrac{q_2}{0.5} \right)$

When $q_3$ is moved to point D along the circular path centered at A, the distance AD is equal to the radius of the path:
$AD = AC = 40\text{ cm} = 0.4\text{ m}$

The distance BD is:
$BD = AD - AB = 0.4\text{ m} - 0.3\text{ m} = 0.1\text{ m}$

The final potential energy of the system when $q_3$ is at point D is:

$U_D = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \left( \dfrac{q_1 q_3}{AD} + \dfrac{q_2 q_3}{BD} \right) = \dfrac{q_3}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \left( \dfrac{q_1}{0.4} + \dfrac{q_2}{0.1} \right)$

The difference in potential energy is:

$\Delta U = U_D - U_C = \dfrac{q_3}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \left( \dfrac{q_1}{0.4} + \dfrac{q_2}{0.1} - \dfrac{q_1}{0.4} - \dfrac{q_2}{0.5} \right)$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{q_3}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \left( \dfrac{q_2}{0.1} - \dfrac{q_2}{0.5} \right)$

$\Delta U = \dfrac{q_3 q_2}{4\pi\varepsilon_0} \left( 10 - 2 \right) = \dfrac{q_3 (8q_2)}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}$

We are given that the difference in potential energy is $\dfrac{q_3 k}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}$.

Comparing the two expressions, we get:
$k = 8q_2$

Answer: $8q_2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electric dipole of length $0.5\ \mu\text{m}$ is placed with its axis making an angle of $30^\circ$ with uniform electric field $10^4\ \text{V/m}$. If it experiences a torque of $5 \times 10^{-9}\ \text{Nm}$, the magnitude of the charge on the dipole is ($\sin 30^\circ = 0.5$)
questions.solution:
The torque experienced by an electric dipole in a uniform electric field is given by

$\tau = pE \sin\theta$

where $p = qd$ is the dipole moment, $q$ is the magnitude of the charge, and $d$ is the length of the dipole.

Substituting $p$ in the torque equation gives

$\tau = q d E \sin\theta$

Rearranging for $q$ yields

$q = \dfrac{\tau}{d E \sin\theta}$

Substituting the given values $\tau = 5 \times 10^{-9}\ \text{Nm}$, $d = 0.5 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{m}$, $E = 10^4\ \text{V/m}$, and $\theta = 30^\circ$:

$q = \dfrac{5 \times 10^{-9}}{0.5 \times 10^{-6} \times 10^4 \times \sin 30^\circ}$

$q = \dfrac{5 \times 10^{-9}}{0.5 \times 10^{-2} \times 0.5}$

$q = \dfrac{5 \times 10^{-9}}{0.25 \times 10^{-2}}$

$q = 20 \times 10^{-7}\ \text{C}$

$q = 2 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{C} = 2\ \mu\text{C}$

Answer: $2\ \mu\text{C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two spherical hollow spheres of radii '$R_1$' and '$R_2$' are charged with same charge. Let '$\sigma_1$' and '$\sigma_2$' are their respective charge densities, then the ratio $\sigma_1$ to $\sigma_2$ is
questions.solution:
Let the charge on both the hollow spheres be $Q$.

The surface charge density $\sigma$ of a sphere of radius $R$ is given by $\sigma = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi R^2}$.

For the first sphere of radius $R_1$, the charge density is $\sigma_1 = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi R_1^2}$.

For the second sphere of radius $R_2$, the charge density is $\sigma_2 = \dfrac{Q}{4\pi R_2^2}$.

Taking the ratio of their charge densities:

$\dfrac{\sigma_1}{\sigma_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{Q}{4\pi R_1^2}}{\dfrac{Q}{4\pi R_2^2}} = \dfrac{R_2^2}{R_1^2}$

Thus, the ratio $\sigma_1 : \sigma_2$ is $R_2^2 : R_1^2$.

Answer: $R_2^2 : R_1^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass m is taken from earth surface to a height h equal to twice the radius of earth, the increase in potential energy will be ($g$ = acceleration due to gravity on earth's surface) (R - radius of earth)
questions.solution:
Initial potential energy of the body on the surface of the earth is $U_i = -\dfrac{GMm}{R}$

Final potential energy of the body at height $h = 2R$ is $U_f = -\dfrac{GMm}{R+h} = -\dfrac{GMm}{R+2R} = -\dfrac{GMm}{3R}$

Increase in potential energy is $\Delta U = U_f - U_i = -\dfrac{GMm}{3R} - \left(-\dfrac{GMm}{R}\right) = \dfrac{2GMm}{3R}$

Using the relation $g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2}$, we have $GM = gR^2$

Substituting this in the expression for $\Delta U$, we get $\Delta U = \dfrac{2(gR^2)m}{3R} = \dfrac{2}{3}mgR$

Answer: $\dfrac{2}{3}\text{mgR}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If a gas is compressed isothermally then the r.m.s. velocity of the molecules
questions.solution:
The root mean square (r.m.s.) velocity of gas molecules is given by the formula $v_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3RT}{M}}$, where $R$ is the universal gas constant, $T$ is the absolute temperature, and $M$ is the molar mass of the gas.

In an isothermal process, the temperature $T$ of the gas remains constant.

Since $v_{rms}$ depends only on the absolute temperature for a given gas, it remains the same during isothermal compression.

Answer: remains the same

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rigid diatomic gas having molar mass m is contained in an insulated container. The container is moving with velocity V. If it is stopped suddenly, the change in temperature is (R - gas constant)
questions.solution:
Let $n$ be the number of moles of the gas. The total mass of the gas is $nm$.

The initial kinetic energy of the gas due to the motion of the container is $K = \dfrac{1}{2}(nm)V^2$.

When the container is suddenly stopped, this kinetic energy is completely converted into the internal energy of the gas because the container is insulated.

The change in internal energy is given by $\Delta U = nC_v\Delta T$.

For a rigid diatomic gas, the molar heat capacity at constant volume is $C_v = \dfrac{5}{2}R$.

Equating the kinetic energy to the change in internal energy:

$\dfrac{1}{2}nmV^2 = n\left(\dfrac{5}{2}R\right)\Delta T$

$\dfrac{1}{2}mV^2 = \dfrac{5}{2}R\Delta T$

$\Delta T = \dfrac{mV^2}{5R}$

Answer: $\dfrac{mV^2}{5R}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The average transnational kinetic energy of a molecule in a gas is $E_1$. The kinetic energy of the electron (e) accelerated from rest through potential difference 'V' volt is $E_2$. The temperature at which $E_1 = E_2$ possible is (mass of molecule and electron is same) (N = number of molecules, V = Velocity, R = gas constant)
questions.solution:
The average translational kinetic energy of a single molecule in a gas is given by:

$E_1 = \dfrac{3}{2} k_B T$

The kinetic energy of an electron accelerated from rest through a potential difference $V$ is:

$E_2 = eV$

Given that $E_1 = E_2$, we have:

$\dfrac{3}{2} k_B T = eV$

$T = \dfrac{2eV}{3k_B}$

We know that the Boltzmann constant $k_B$ is related to the universal gas constant $R$ and Avogadro's number $N$ by the relation $k_B = \dfrac{R}{N}$. Substituting this into the equation for $T$, we get:

$T = \dfrac{2eV}{3 \left(\dfrac{R}{N}\right)}$

$T = \dfrac{2VNe}{3R}$

Answer: $\dfrac{2VNe}{3R}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular loop of radius R is carrying current I. The ratio of magnetic field at the center of circular loop and at a distance R from the center of the loop on its axis is
questions.solution:
The magnetic field at the center of a circular loop of radius $R$ carrying current $I$ is given by:

$B_{center} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}$

The magnetic field on the axis of the circular loop at a distance $x$ from the center is given by:

$B_{axis} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$

Substituting $x = R$, we get:

$B_{axis} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + R^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(2R^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(2\sqrt{2}R^3)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\sqrt{2}R}$

The ratio of the magnetic fields is:

$\dfrac{B_{center}}{B_{axis}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2R}}{\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\sqrt{2}R}} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{2} = 2\sqrt{2} = \sqrt{8}$

The required ratio is $\sqrt{8} : 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnitude of magnetic induction at mid point 'O' due to current arrangement as shown in figure will be ($\mu_0$ = permeability of free space)
questions.solution:
From the given figure, the horizontal distance between the vertical wire segment BC and the vertical wire segment ET is $a$.

Since point O is the midpoint, the perpendicular distance from O to each of these vertical segments is $a/2$.

Assuming the horizontal wire segments AB and DE are collinear and their extended axis passes through O, the magnetic field produced by them at point O is zero.

The vertical segment BC acts as a semi-infinite straight wire with its end at the level of O. The magnetic induction at O due to BC is $B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi(a/2)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a}$. By the right-hand thumb rule, its direction is perpendicular to the plane of the paper, pointing outwards.

The vertical segment ET also acts as a semi-infinite straight wire with its end at the level of O. The magnetic induction at O due to ET is $B_2 = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{4\pi(a/2)} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a}$. By the right-hand thumb rule, its direction is also perpendicular to the plane of the paper, pointing outwards.

Since both magnetic fields are in the same direction, the total magnetic induction at O is the sum of their magnitudes:

$B = B_1 + B_2$

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a} + \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi a} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{\pi a}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic field intensity (H) at the centre of a long solenoid having 'n' turns per unit length and carrying a current I, when no material is kept in it is ($\mu_0$ = permeability of free space)
questions.solution:
The magnetic field $B$ at the centre of a long solenoid is given by $B = \mu_0 n I$, where $n$ is the number of turns per unit length and $I$ is the current.

The magnetic field intensity $H$ is related to the magnetic field $B$ in free space by the relation $H = \dfrac{B}{\mu_0}$.

Substituting the value of $B$, we get $H = \dfrac{\mu_0 n I}{\mu_0} = nI$.

Answer: $nI$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Vectors $a\hat{i} + b\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$ are perpendicular to each other when $3a + 2b = 7$, the ratio of a to b is $x/2$. The value of x is
questions.solution:
Let the given vectors be $\vec{p} = a\hat{i} + b\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $\vec{q} = 2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}$.

Since the vectors are perpendicular, their dot product is zero:

$\vec{p} \cdot \vec{q} = 0$

$2a - 3b + 4 = 0$

$2a - 3b = -4$

We are given another equation:

$3a + 2b = 7$

Solving the two equations simultaneously, multiply the first by $2$ and the second by $3$:

$4a - 6b = -8$

$9a + 6b = 21$

Adding both equations:

$13a = 13 \Rightarrow a = 1$

Substituting $a = 1$ in $3a + 2b = 7$:

$3(1) + 2b = 7 \Rightarrow 2b = 4 \Rightarrow b = 2$

The ratio of $a$ to $b$ is $\dfrac{a}{b} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Given that the ratio is $\dfrac{x}{2}$, we have:

$\dfrac{x}{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow x = 1$

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The error in the measurement of length and mass of a cube is 3% and 4% respectively. The error in the measurement of its density will be
questions.solution:
Density of a cube is given by $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V} = \dfrac{M}{L^3}$

The maximum percentage error in density is

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = \dfrac{\Delta M}{M} \times 100 + 3 \left( \dfrac{\Delta L}{L} \times 100 \right)$

Given $\dfrac{\Delta M}{M} \times 100 = 4\%$ and $\dfrac{\Delta L}{L} \times 100 = 3\%$

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = 4\% + 3(3\%) = 4\% + 9\% = 13\%$

Answer: $13\ \%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A horizontal pipe carries water in a streamline flow. At point along the pipe, where the cross-sectional area is $A_1$, the velocity of water is $V_1$ and the pressure is $P_1$. What is the pressure of water at another point where the cross-sectional area is $A_2$?
questions.solution:
Using the equation of continuity:

$A_1 V_1 = A_2 V_2 \Rightarrow V_2 = \dfrac{A_1 V_1}{A_2}$

Using Bernoulli's theorem for a horizontal pipe:

$P_1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\varrho V_1^2 = P_2 + \dfrac{1}{2}\varrho V_2^2$

$P_2 = P_1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\varrho (V_1^2 - V_2^2)$

Substituting the value of $V_2$:

$P_2 = P_1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\varrho \left(V_1^2 - \dfrac{A_1^2 V_1^2}{A_2^2}\right)$

$P_2 = P_1 + \dfrac{\varrho V_1^2}{2A_2^2}(A_2^2 - A_1^2)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Under isothermal condition, two soap bubbles of radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ combine to form a single soap bubble of radius R. The surface tension of the soap solution is (P = outside pressure)
questions.solution:
Let $T$ be the surface tension of the soap solution.

The pressure inside a soap bubble of radius $r$ is given by $P_i = P + \dfrac{4T}{r}$, where $P$ is the outside pressure.

The volume of the bubble is $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$.

Under isothermal conditions, the temperature remains constant. The total number of moles of air inside the bubbles is conserved, which gives $P_1 V_1 + P_2 V_2 = P_f V_f$.

Substituting the values for the two initial bubbles and the final bubble:

$\left(P + \dfrac{4T}{r_1}\right) \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r_1^3 + \left(P + \dfrac{4T}{r_2}\right) \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r_2^3 = \left(P + \dfrac{4T}{R}\right) \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3$

Dividing the entire equation by $\dfrac{4}{3}\pi$:

$P r_1^3 + 4T r_1^2 + P r_2^3 + 4T r_2^2 = P R^3 + 4T R^2$

Rearranging the terms to solve for $T$:

$4T r_1^2 + 4T r_2^2 - 4T R^2 = P R^3 - P r_1^3 - P r_2^3$

$4T (r_1^2 + r_2^2 - R^2) = P (R^3 - r_1^3 - r_2^3)$

$T = \dfrac{P(R^3 - r_1^3 - r_2^3)}{4(r_1^2 + r_2^2 - R^2)}$

Answer: $\dfrac{P(R^3 - r_1^3 - r_2^3)}{4(r_1^2 + r_2^2 - R^2)}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One thousand small water drops of equal radii combine to form a big drop. The ratio of final surface energy to the total initial surface energy is
questions.solution:
Let $r$ be the radius of each small drop and $R$ be the radius of the big drop.

Since volume remains constant during the combination of drops:

$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 1000 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$

$R = 10r$

Initial total surface energy of $1000$ drops is:

$E_i = 1000 \times 4\pi r^2 T$

Final surface energy of the big drop is:

$E_f = 4\pi R^2 T = 4\pi (10r)^2 T = 100 \times 4\pi r^2 T$

The ratio of final surface energy to the total initial surface energy is:

$\dfrac{E_f}{E_i} = \dfrac{100 \times 4\pi r^2 T}{1000 \times 4\pi r^2 T} = \dfrac{1}{10}$

The ratio is $1 : 10$.

Answer: $1 : 10$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two objects are projected with same velocity 'u' at different angles $\alpha$ and $\beta$ with the horizontal. If $\alpha + \beta = 90^\circ$, the ratio of horizontal range of the first object to the second object will be $[\sin(\pi - \theta) = \sin\theta]$
questions.solution:
The horizontal range of a projectile is given by $R = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\theta)}{g}$.

For the first object projected at angle $\alpha$, the range is $R_1 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\alpha)}{g}$.

For the second object projected at angle $\beta$, the range is $R_2 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\beta)}{g}$.

Given $\alpha + \beta = 90^\circ$, we have $\beta = 90^\circ - \alpha$.

Substituting $\beta$ in the expression for $R_2$:

$R_2 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2(90^\circ - \alpha))}{g} = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(180^\circ - 2\alpha)}{g}$

Using the identity $\sin(180^\circ - \theta) = \sin\theta$, we get:

$R_2 = \dfrac{u^2 \sin(2\alpha)}{g}$

Thus, $R_1 = R_2$, which means the ratio of their horizontal ranges is $1 : 1$.

Answer: $1 : 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The ratio of the density of oxygen nucleus $({}^{16}_{8}\text{O})$ and helium nucleus $({}^{4}_{2}\text{He})$ is
questions.solution:
The radius of a nucleus with mass number $A$ is given by $R = R_0 A^{1/3}$.

The volume of the nucleus is $V = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R^3 = \dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3 A$.

The mass of the nucleus is $M \approx A m$, where $m$ is the average mass of a nucleon.

The density of the nucleus is $\rho = \dfrac{M}{V} = \dfrac{A m}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3 A} = \dfrac{m}{\dfrac{4}{3} \pi R_0^3}$.

Since the density is independent of the mass number $A$, it is constant for all nuclei.

Therefore, the ratio of the density of the oxygen nucleus to the helium nucleus is $1 : 1$.

Answer: $1 : 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The time taken by simple pendulum for one oscillation is T on earth's surface. Its time period becomes xT when taken to a height R (equal to earth's radius) above the earth's surface. The value of x is
questions.solution:
The time period of a simple pendulum on the surface of the earth is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$.

The acceleration due to gravity at a height $h$ above the earth's surface is $g' = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + \dfrac{h}{R}\right)^2}$.

Given $h = R$, we have $g' = \dfrac{g}{\left(1 + \dfrac{R}{R}\right)^2} = \dfrac{g}{4}$.

The new time period $T'$ at height $R$ is $T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g'}} = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{\dfrac{g}{4}}} = 2 \times 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}} = 2T$.

Since $T' = xT$, we get $x = 2$.

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The maximum potential energy of a block executing S.H.M. is E and amplitude of oscillation is 'A'. The kinetic energy of the block at amplitude A/2 is
questions.solution:
The maximum potential energy of a block executing simple harmonic motion is given by $E = \dfrac{1}{2} k A^2$, which is also equal to the total energy of the system.

The kinetic energy of the block at any displacement $x$ is given by $K = \dfrac{1}{2} k (A^2 - x^2)$.

Substituting $x = \dfrac{A}{2}$ into the kinetic energy expression:

$K = \dfrac{1}{2} k \left(A^2 - \left(\dfrac{A}{2}\right)^2\right)$

$K = \dfrac{1}{2} k \left(A^2 - \dfrac{A^2}{4}\right)$

$K = \dfrac{1}{2} k \left(\dfrac{3A^2}{4}\right)$

$K = \dfrac{3}{4} \left(\dfrac{1}{2} k A^2\right)$

Since $E = \dfrac{1}{2} k A^2$, we get:

$K = \dfrac{3\text{E}}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3\text{E}}{4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mass $m_1$ performs S.H.M. with amplitude A which is connected to horizontal spring. While mass $m_1$ passing through mean position, another mass $m_2$ ($m_2 \lt  m_1$) is placed on it so that both masses move together with amplitude $A_1$. The ratio of $A/A_1$ is
questions.solution:
Velocity of mass $m_1$ at the mean position is given by $v = A\omega = A\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m_1}}$.

When mass $m_2$ is placed on $m_1$, the horizontal momentum of the system is conserved.

$m_1 v = (m_1 + m_2)v_1$

$v_1 = \dfrac{m_1 v}{m_1 + m_2}$

The new angular frequency of the system is $\omega_1 = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m_1 + m_2}}$.

The new amplitude $A_1$ is related to the new maximum velocity $v_1$ by $v_1 = A_1 \omega_1$.

Substituting the values of $v_1$ and $\omega_1$:

$A_1 \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m_1 + m_2}} = \dfrac{m_1}{m_1 + m_2} A \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m_1}}$

$A_1 = A \dfrac{m_1}{m_1 + m_2} \sqrt{\dfrac{m_1 + m_2}{m_1}}$

$A_1 = A \sqrt{\dfrac{m_1}{m_1 + m_2}}$

Rearranging to find the ratio $\dfrac{A}{A_1}$:

$\dfrac{A}{A_1} = \left[\dfrac{m_1 + m_2}{m_1}\right]^{\dfrac{1}{2}}$

Answer: $\left[\dfrac{m_1 + m_2}{m_1}\right]^{\frac{1}{2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A convex lens having refractive index 1.6 has focal length 12 cm, when it is in air. The focal length of that lens when placed in water is (refractive index of water = 1.28)
questions.solution:
Using the Lens Maker's formula for the lens in air:

$\dfrac{1}{f_a} = (\mu_g - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{12} = (1.6 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{12} = 0.6 \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)$

Using the Lens Maker's formula for the lens in water:

$\dfrac{1}{f_w} = \left( \dfrac{\mu_g}{\mu_w} - 1 \right) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f_w} = \left( \dfrac{1.6}{1.28} - 1 \right) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f_w} = (1.25 - 1) \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{f_w} = 0.25 \left( \dfrac{1}{R_1} - \dfrac{1}{R_2} \right)$

Dividing the two equations:

$\dfrac{f_w}{f_a} = \dfrac{0.6}{0.25}$

$f_w = 12 \times 2.4 = 28.8\ \text{cm}$

$f_w = 288\ \text{mm}$

Answer: $288\ \text{mm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray of light passes from the vacuum into a medium of refractive index 'n'. If the angle of incidence is twice the angle of refraction, then the angle of incidence in terms of refractive index is
questions.solution:
Let the angle of incidence be $i$ and the angle of refraction be $r$.

Given that the angle of incidence is twice the angle of refraction:

$i = 2r$

According to Snell's law:

$\sin(i) = n \sin(r)$

Substituting $i = 2r$ into the equation:

$\sin(2r) = n \sin(r)$

Using the double angle formula $\sin(2r) = 2 \sin(r) \cos(r)$:

$2 \sin(r) \cos(r) = n \sin(r)$

Assuming $r \neq 0$, dividing both sides by $\sin(r)$ gives:

$2 \cos(r) = n$

$\cos(r) = \dfrac{n}{2}$

$r = \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{n}{2}\right)$

Since the angle of incidence is $i = 2r$, we get:

$i = 2\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{n}{2}\right)$

Answer: $2\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{n}{2}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Solid sphere is rotating about an axis as shown in figure. If the radius of the sphere is 5 cm, then radius of gyration about that axis will be $\sqrt{x}$ cm. The value of x is
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of a solid sphere about an axis passing through its center of mass is given by $I_{cm} = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$.

Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia about the given axis of rotation is:

$I = I_{cm} + Md^2$

where $d$ is the distance from the axis of rotation to the center of mass of the sphere.

Given $R = 5$ cm and $d = 10$ cm, we have:

$I = \dfrac{2}{5}M(5)^2 + M(10)^2$

$I = 10M + 100M = 110M$

The radius of gyration $k$ is defined by $I = Mk^2$.

$Mk^2 = 110M$

$k^2 = 110$

$k = \sqrt{110}$ cm

Comparing this with $\sqrt{x}$ cm, we get $x = 110$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform solid cylinder with radius R and length L has moment of inertia $I_1$ about the axis of the cylinder. A concentric solid cylinder of radius $R/2$ and length $L/2$ is carved out of the original cylinder. If $I_2$ is the moment of inertia of the carved out portion of the cylinder then $I_1/I_2$ is (Both $I_1$ and $I_2$ are about the axis of the cylinder)
questions.solution:
Let the density of the material of the cylinder be $\rho$.

The mass of the original solid cylinder is $M_1 = \rho \pi R^2 L$.
The moment of inertia of the original solid cylinder about its axis is:
$I_1 = \dfrac{1}{2} M_1 R^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} (\rho \pi R^2 L) R^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \rho \pi R^4 L$

The carved out portion is a solid cylinder of radius $R/2$ and length $L/2$. Its mass is:
$M_2 = \rho \pi \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)^2 \left(\dfrac{L}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{8} \rho \pi R^2 L$

The moment of inertia of this carved out portion about the same axis is:
$I_2 = \dfrac{1}{2} M_2 \left(\dfrac{R}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{1}{8} \rho \pi R^2 L\right) \left(\dfrac{R^2}{4}\right) = \dfrac{1}{64} \rho \pi R^4 L$

Taking the ratio of $I_1$ to $I_2$:
$\dfrac{I_1}{I_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} \rho \pi R^4 L}{\dfrac{1}{64} \rho \pi R^4 L} = 32$

Thus, the ratio is $32 : 1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of mass M and a disc of mass $\dfrac{M}{2}$ have the same radius. The ratio of moment of inertia of the disc about a tangent in its plane to the moment of inertia of the sphere about its tangent will be
questions.solution:
Let the radius of the solid sphere and the disc be $R$.

Mass of the solid sphere, $m_{s} = M$

Mass of the disc, $m_{d} = \dfrac{M}{2}$

Moment of inertia of the disc about its diameter is $\dfrac{1}{4}m_{d}R^2$. Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of the disc about a tangent in its plane is:

$I_{disc} = \dfrac{1}{4}m_{d}R^2 + m_{d}R^2 = \dfrac{5}{4}m_{d}R^2$

Substituting $m_{d} = \dfrac{M}{2}$:

$I_{disc} = \dfrac{5}{4}\left(\dfrac{M}{2}\right)R^2 = \dfrac{5}{8}MR^2$

Moment of inertia of the solid sphere about its diameter is $\dfrac{2}{5}m_{s}R^2$. Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of the solid sphere about its tangent is:

$I_{sphere} = \dfrac{2}{5}m_{s}R^2 + m_{s}R^2 = \dfrac{7}{5}m_{s}R^2$

Substituting $m_{s} = M$:

$I_{sphere} = \dfrac{7}{5}MR^2$

The required ratio is:

$\dfrac{I_{disc}}{I_{sphere}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{5}{8}MR^2}{\dfrac{7}{5}MR^2} = \dfrac{5}{8} \times \dfrac{5}{7} = \dfrac{25}{56}$

Answer: $25 : 56$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In which of the logic gate the following statement is true? "The output is high when either of the inputs is high but not if both inputs are high"
questions.solution:
The given statement states that the output is high ($1$) when either of the inputs is high ($1$), but the output is low ($0$) if both inputs are high ($1$).

This corresponds to the following truth table:
$A = 0, B = 0 \Rightarrow Y = 0$
$A = 1, B = 0 \Rightarrow Y = 1$
$A = 0, B = 1 \Rightarrow Y = 1$
$A = 1, B = 1 \Rightarrow Y = 0$

This is the characteristic truth table of an Exclusive-OR (X-OR) gate.

Answer: X-OR

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Which of the following statement is NOT correct in the case of LED?
(A) It is a heavily doped p-n junction diode.
(B) It emits light only when it is forward biased.
(C) It emits light only when it is reverse biased.
(D) The energy of the light emitted is equal to or slightly less than the energy gap of the semiconductor used.
questions.solution:
A Light Emitting Diode (LED) is a heavily doped p-n junction diode which under forward bias emits spontaneous radiation.

When the diode is forward biased, electrons are sent from n \rightarrow p (where they are minority carriers) and holes are sent from p \rightarrow n (where they are minority carriers). At the junction boundary, the concentration of minority carriers increases compared to the equilibrium concentration. Thus, at the junction boundary on either side of the junction, excess minority carriers are there which recombine with majority carriers near the junction.

On recombination, the energy is released in the form of photons. Photons with energy equal to or slightly less than the band gap are emitted.

Therefore, an LED emits light only when it is forward biased. The statement that it emits light only when it is reverse biased is incorrect.

Answer: C

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Electrical conductivity of insulators is
questions.solution:
Insulators are materials that offer very high resistance to the flow of electric current. Their energy band gap is very large (typically greater than $3 \text{ eV}$), which means there are almost no free electrons available for conduction at room temperature.

As a result, the electrical conductivity of insulators is not exactly zero but is extremely small, typically in the range of $10^{-20}$ to $10^{-10} \, \Omega^{-1} \text{m}^{-1}$.

Answer: extremely small

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bowl filled with very hot water cools from $98^\circ\text{C}$ to $86^\circ\text{C}$ in 2 minutes when the room temperature is $22^\circ\text{C}$. How long it will take to cool from $75^\circ\text{C}$ to $69^\circ\text{C}$ ?
questions.solution:
Using Newton's law of cooling:

$\dfrac{T_1 - T_2}{t} = K \left( \dfrac{T_1 + T_2}{2} - T_0 \right)$

For the first case:

$\dfrac{98 - 86}{2} = K \left( \dfrac{98 + 86}{2} - 22 \right)$

$6 = K (92 - 22)$

$6 = 70K \Rightarrow K = \dfrac{3}{35}$

For the second case:

$\dfrac{75 - 69}{t} = K \left( \dfrac{75 + 69}{2} - 22 \right)$

$\dfrac{6}{t} = K (72 - 22)$

$\dfrac{6}{t} = 50K$

Substituting the value of $K$:

$\dfrac{6}{t} = 50 \times \dfrac{3}{35}$

$\dfrac{6}{t} = \dfrac{30}{7}$

$t = \dfrac{42}{30} = 1.4 \text{ minutes}$

Answer: $1.4$ minute

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One gram of a liquid is converted to vapour at $3 \times 10^5$ Pa pressure. If 10% of the heat supplied is used for increasing the volume by $1600\ \text{cm}^3$ during this phase change, then the increase in internal energy in the process will be
questions.solution:
The work done during the phase change is given by $W = P \Delta V$.

Substituting the given values, $W = (3 \times 10^5) \times (1600 \times 10^{-6}) = 480\ \text{J}$.

It is given that $10\%$ of the heat supplied is used for increasing the volume, which means $W = 0.1 Q$.

Therefore, the total heat supplied is $Q = \dfrac{W}{0.1} = \dfrac{480}{0.1} = 4800\ \text{J}$.

According to the first law of thermodynamics, $Q = \Delta U + W$.

The increase in internal energy is $\Delta U = Q - W = 4800 - 480 = 4320\ \text{J}$.

Answer: $4320\ \text{J}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A Carnot engine with efficiency 50% takes heat from a source at 600 K. To increase the efficiency by 20%, keeping temperature of the sink same, the new temperature of the source will be
questions.solution:
The efficiency of a Carnot engine is given by $\eta = 1 - \dfrac{T_2}{T_1}$, where $T_1$ is the source temperature and $T_2$ is the sink temperature.

Given initial efficiency $\eta_1 = 50\% = 0.5$ and source temperature $T_1 = 600\ \text{K}$.

$0.5 = 1 - \dfrac{T_2}{600}$

$\dfrac{T_2}{600} = 0.5 \Rightarrow T_2 = 300\ \text{K}$

The efficiency is increased by $20\%$, so the new efficiency is $\eta_2 = 50\% + 20\% = 70\% = 0.7$.

Let the new source temperature be $T_1'$. The sink temperature $T_2$ remains the same.

$0.7 = 1 - \dfrac{300}{T_1'}$

$\dfrac{300}{T_1'} = 0.3$

$T_1' = \dfrac{300}{0.3} = 1000\ \text{K}$

Answer: $1000\ \text{K}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
In Young's double slit experiment, two slits are illuminated with a light of wavelength $\lambda$. The line joining $A_1P$ is perpendicular to $A_1A_2$ as shown in figure. If the first minimum is detected at P, the value of slits separation 'a' will be
(D = distance between source and screen)
questions.solution:
From the given figure, the path difference at point P is given by:

$\Delta x = A_2P - A_1P$

Using Pythagoras theorem in right-angled triangle $A_1A_2P$, we have $A_1P = D$ and $A_2P = \sqrt{D^2 + a^2}$.

So, $\Delta x = \sqrt{D^2 + a^2} - D$

For the first minimum to be detected at P, the path difference must be $\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$.

$\sqrt{D^2 + a^2} - D = \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

$\sqrt{D^2 + a^2} = D + \dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

Squaring both sides, we get:

$D^2 + a^2 = D^2 + D\lambda + \dfrac{\lambda^2}{4}$

$a^2 = D\lambda + \dfrac{\lambda^2}{4}$

Since the wavelength of light $\lambda$ is very small compared to the distance $D$ ($\lambda \ll D$), the term $\dfrac{\lambda^2}{4}$ is negligibly small and can be ignored.

$a^2 \approx D\lambda$

$a = \sqrt{\lambda D}$

Answer: $\sqrt{\lambda\text{D}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Three identical polaroids $P_1$, $P_2$ and $P_3$ are placed one after another. The pass axis of $P_2$ and $P_3$ are inclined at angle of $60^\circ$ and $90^\circ$ with respect to axis of $P_1$. The source has an intensity $I_0$. The intensity of light finally coming out is
questions.solution:
Initial intensity of unpolarized light from the source is $I_0$.

After passing through the first polaroid $P_1$, the intensity becomes $I_1 = \dfrac{I_0}{2}$.

The angle between the pass axes of $P_1$ and $P_2$ is $\theta_1 = 60^\circ$. By Malus's law, the intensity after passing through $P_2$ is $I_2 = I_1 \cos^2 \theta_1 = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \cos^2 60^\circ$.

The pass axis of $P_3$ is at an angle of $90^\circ$ with respect to $P_1$. The angle between the pass axes of $P_2$ and $P_3$ is $\theta_2 = 90^\circ - 60^\circ = 30^\circ$.

The intensity after passing through $P_3$ is $I_3 = I_2 \cos^2 \theta_2 = \dfrac{I_0}{2} \cos^2 60^\circ \cos^2 30^\circ$.

Answer: $\dfrac{I_0}{2}\cos^2 60^\circ\cos^2 30^\circ$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person observes two moving trains. 'A' reaching the station and 'B' leaving the station with equal speed of 30m/s. If both trains emit sounds with frequency 300 Hz, (speed of sound = 330 m/s) difference of frequencies heard by the person will be
questions.solution:
Given:
Speed of sound, $v = 330\ \text{m/s}$
Speed of trains, $v_s = 30\ \text{m/s}$
Actual frequency, $f_0 = 300\ \text{Hz}$

Apparent frequency of train A (moving towards the observer):
$f_A = f_0 \left( \dfrac{v}{v - v_s} \right)$
$f_A = 300 \left( \dfrac{330}{330 - 30} \right) = 300 \left( \dfrac{330}{300} \right) = 330\ \text{Hz}$

Apparent frequency of train B (moving away from the observer):
$f_B = f_0 \left( \dfrac{v}{v + v_s} \right)$
$f_B = 300 \left( \dfrac{330}{330 + 30} \right) = 300 \left( \dfrac{330}{360} \right) = 275\ \text{Hz}$

Difference in frequencies heard by the person:
$\Delta f = f_A - f_B = 330 - 275 = 55\ \text{Hz}$

Answer: $55\ \text{Hz}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When open pipe is closed from one end then third overtone of closed pipe is higher in frequency by 150Hz than second overtone of open pipe. The fundamental frequency of open end pipe will be (Neglect end correction)
questions.solution:
Let the fundamental frequency of the open pipe be $f_o = \dfrac{v}{2L}$.

The frequency of the second overtone of the open pipe corresponds to the third harmonic, so $f_{o2} = 3f_o$.

When the pipe is closed at one end, its fundamental frequency becomes $f_c = \dfrac{v}{4L} = \dfrac{f_o}{2}$.

The frequency of the third overtone of the closed pipe corresponds to the seventh harmonic, so $f_{c3} = 7f_c = 7\left(\dfrac{f_o}{2}\right) = 3.5f_o$.

Given that the third overtone of the closed pipe is higher in frequency by $150\text{ Hz}$ than the second overtone of the open pipe:

$f_{c3} - f_{o2} = 150$

$3.5f_o - 3f_o = 150$

$0.5f_o = 150$

$f_o = 300\text{ Hz}$

Answer: $300\ \text{Hz}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two waves $Y_1 = 0.25\sin 316t$ and $Y_2 = 0.25\sin 310t$ are propagating along the same direction. The number of beats produced per second are
questions.solution:
Given equations of waves are $Y_1 = 0.25\sin 316t$ and $Y_2 = 0.25\sin 310t$.

Comparing with the standard wave equation $Y = A\sin \omega t$, the angular frequencies are:

$\omega_1 = 316$ rad/s

$\omega_2 = 310$ rad/s

The corresponding frequencies are:

$f_1 = \dfrac{\omega_1}{2\pi} = \dfrac{316}{2\pi} = \dfrac{158}{\pi}$ Hz

$f_2 = \dfrac{\omega_2}{2\pi} = \dfrac{310}{2\pi} = \dfrac{155}{\pi}$ Hz

The number of beats produced per second is given by the difference in frequencies:

$f_{beat} = f_1 - f_2 = \dfrac{158}{\pi} - \dfrac{155}{\pi} = \dfrac{3}{\pi}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{\pi}$

questions.q: An air column in a pipe which is closed at one end will be in resonance with a vibrating tuning fork of frequency 415 Hz for various vibrating air columns. Which one of the following lengths is not in resonance ? (velocity of sound in air = 332 m/s) (Neglect end correction)
questions.solution:
Given frequency $f = 415 \text{ Hz}$ and velocity $v = 332 \text{ m/s}$.

The wavelength of the sound wave is:

$\lambda = \dfrac{v}{f} = \dfrac{332}{415} \text{ m}$

$\lambda = 0.8 \text{ m} = 80 \text{ cm}$

For a pipe closed at one end, the resonating lengths are given by odd multiples of $\dfrac{\lambda}{4}$:

$L = (2n - 1)\dfrac{\lambda}{4}$ where $n = 1, 2, 3, \dots$

The possible resonating lengths are:

$L_1 = 1 \times \dfrac{80}{4} = 20 \text{ cm}$

$L_2 = 3 \times \dfrac{80}{4} = 60 \text{ cm}$

$L_3 = 5 \times \dfrac{80}{4} = 100 \text{ cm}$

Among the given options, $40 \text{ cm}$ is an even multiple of $\dfrac{\lambda}{4}$ and therefore is not a resonating length.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body of mass 1kg begins to move under the action of a time dependent force $\vec{F} = (t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j})\ \text{N}$ where $\hat{i}$ and $\hat{j}$ are the unit vectors along x and y axis. The power developed by the above force at time $t = 2\ \text{s}$ will be (in watt)
questions.solution:
Given $\vec{F} = t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j}$ and $m = 1\ \text{kg}$.

Acceleration $\vec{a} = \dfrac{\vec{F}}{m} = t\hat{i} + 3t^2\hat{j}$

Velocity $\vec{v} = \int \vec{a} dt = \dfrac{t^2}{2}\hat{i} + t^3\hat{j}$ (since the body begins to move from rest, $\vec{v}(0) = 0$).

At $t = 2\ \text{s}$:

$\vec{F} = 2\hat{i} + 3(2)^2\hat{j} = 2\hat{i} + 12\hat{j}$

$\vec{v} = \dfrac{2^2}{2}\hat{i} + (2)^3\hat{j} = 2\hat{i} + 8\hat{j}$

Power $P = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{v} = (2\hat{i} + 12\hat{j}) \cdot (2\hat{i} + 8\hat{j})$

$P = (2 \times 2) + (12 \times 8) = 4 + 96 = 100\ \text{W}$

Answer: $100$
